Rhinoceros, s. gaMqaH, gaMqakaH, Kaqgin m.; ‘the female r(hinoceros)’ KaqgaDenuH.
RHINOCEROS: (1) gaRqaH, -kaH;(2) KaNgin (m.: KaNgaH = its horn);(3) tEtilaH (rare). She-r.: KaNgiDenuH, -kA, K. ; etc. (G. § 103).
RHINOCEROS , s. KaNgaH, KaNgI m. (n), ekaSfNgaH, gaRqaH -RqakaH, gaRqANgaH, ekacaraH, vanotsAhaH, tEtilaH; ‘its horn,’ KaNgaH; ‘the female,’ KaNgaDenuH f.
RHOMB , RHOMBUS, s. vizamacaturasraM, vizamacatuzkoRaH.
RHOMBOID: tulyasammuKaBujaScaturBujaH; *vizamAyataH.
Rhombus, s. tulyacaturBujaH.
RHOMBUS: (1) tulyacaturBujaH, Li. 148.;(2) sama- caturBujaH.
RHUBARB: Kesam (in Mahratti).
RHUBARB , s. revasaM, revAcinI. These are Mahrattī words.
Rhyme, s. yamakaH-kaM, mitrAkzaraM. 2 padyaM, kavitA. [Rhym]er, s. kavitA-padya-kAraH, kukaviH.
RHYME (subs.): I Of verses: mitrAkzaram.II A verse: SlokaH.III Poetry: q. v.: padyam. Ph.: without r. or reason: nizkAraRam, etc.
RHYME (v.): I To accord in sound: perh. mitrIBavati.II To make r.: padyaM karoti: v. Poetry.

RHYME , s. (Correspondence of sounds in poetry) yamakaH -kaM, antyayamakaH -kaM, antyaSabdayamakaH -kaM, antyaSabdasamatA, anuprAsaH, mitrA- kzaraM. — (A word to correspond in sound to another) yamakaSabdaH, yamakaH -kaM. — (Poetry) kavitA, kAvyaM.
To RHYME , v. n. (Correspond in sound) yamakaH -kA -kaM BU, yamaka- Sabdo BU. — (Make rhyme) kavitAM kf, kAvyaM kf, anuprAsaM kf.
RHYMELESS , a. yamakahInaH -nA -naM, ayamakaH -kA -kaM, ananuprAsaH -sA -saM.
RHYMER: (1) kavitAkAraH;(2) kukaviH (= bad poet): v. Versifier.
Rhythm, s. tAlaH, layaH. [Rhythm]ical, a. laya-tAla-anugata; tAlabadDa.
RHYTHM: (1) tAlaH;(2) layaH (= musical time).
RHYTHM , RHYTHMUS, s. tAlaH, layaH, gATA, tAlabanDanaM, tAlabadDatA.
RHYTHMICAL: (1) tAlabadDa (f. dDA);(2) tAlAnugata (f. tA); and sim. comp.s.
RHYTHMICAL , a. tAlabadDaH -dDA -dDaM, layabadDaH &c., tAlasambanDI -nDinI &c.
Rib, s. parSukA, pArSvakaM, pArSvAsTi n.; ‘the r(ib)s taken together’ paMjaraH-raM. 2 poliMdaH. 3 SalAkA (of umbrellas). 4 reKA.
RIB: I Lit.:(1) parSuH, -kA;(2) pArSvakam or pArSvAsTi (n.);(3) paYjaram (= r. s collectively). II Of a boat: polindaH (?).III Of cloth: reKA.

RIB , s. (Bone of an animal) parSukA, pArSukA, parSuH m., pArSvAsTi n., pArSvakaH, vaMkriH m.; ‘the ribs collectively,’ paYjaraM -raH, piYjaraM -raH, pArSvaM. — (Of a boat) polindaH. — (Of an umbrella, &c.) SalAkA, — (A thin slip of wood) SalAkA — (A prominent line) reKA.
RIBALD: durvinIta (f. tA): v. Mean, obscene.
RIBALD , a. durmuKaH -KA -KaM, aSudDaBAzI -ziRI -zi (n), avAcyaBAzI &c., avAcyaH -cyA -cyaM, avadyaH &c., garhyaH -rhyA -rhyaM, duruktaH -ktA -ktaM, kutsitaH -tA -taM.
RIBALDRY: aSlIlatA: v. Obscenity, indecency.
RIBALDRY , s. duruktiH f., durvacanaM, kutsitavAkyaM, avadyaM, avAcyaM, nyaNgaM.
RIBBED , p. p. or a. saSalAkaH -kA -kaM, SalAkI -kinI &c., reKANkitaH -tA -taM.
Ribbon, Riband, s. pawwabaMDaH, dukUlapawwaH.
RIBBON, RIBAND: Perh. pawwabanDaH.
RIBBON , RIBAND, s. pawwaH, dukUlapawwaH, dIrGadukUlaKaRqaH, dIrGapawwaH, banDanI.

Rice, s. (Plant) SAliH, kalamaH, nIvAraH, vrIhiH (various kinds). 2 taMqulaH, DAnyAsTi n. 3 (Boiled) annaM, odanaH-naM, BaktaM; See Food; ‘r(ice) with milk and sugar’ pAyasam, paramAnnaM; ‘scum of r(ice)’ mAsaraH, AcAmaH, nisra(srA)vaH, BaktamaMqaH; ‘scorched r(ice)’ missawA, dagDikA; ‘fried r(ice)’ DAnAH (f. pl.); ‘ear of r(ice)’ kaRiSaH SaM, DAnyaSIrzakaH.

RICE: I The plant:(1) SAliH (= winter r.), red (= table) r.: raktaSAliH; white r.: kalamaH; (2) ASuH (= aus, early r.);(3) vrIhiH (= boro, rice ripening in the rains);(4) zazwikA (= a rice of quick growth);(5) nIvAraH (= a wild rice).II Husked r.: taRqulaH, grains of r.: taRqulakaRAH, H.III. Boiled r.:(1) annam;(2) odanam;(3) anDas,(4) Baktam. Ph.: r. boiled in milk with sugar: pAyasam, paramAnnam; r. boiled with dāl, khichri: kfsarA, Bha.

RICE , s. (The grain in the husk) SAliH m., vrIhiH m., DAnyaM, DAnyottamaM, stambakariH m., jIvasADanaM. — (The grain without the husk, or after threshing) taRqulaH, DAnyAsTi n., DAnyasAraH, SAli- sAraH; ‘a grain of rice,’ taRqulakaRaH. — (Wild rice) nIvAraH; ‘a grain of it,’ nIvArakaRaH. — (A white rice growing in deep water) kalamaH. — (Red sort, growing in moist soil) zazwikaH -kA; ‘fit for growing it,’ zazwikyaH -kyA -kyaM. — (Large or fragrant sort) mahAvrIhiH m., mahASAliH m. — (New rice) navaGAnyaM navAnnaM. One hundred and eighty varieties of rice [Page691-a+ 51] are enumerated. — (Boiled rice) annaM, odanaH -naM, BaktaM, anDas n., BissA, dIdiviH m.; ‘scum of it,’ mAsaraH, AcAmaH, nisrAvaH, visrAvaH. — (Scorched) BissawA, BissiWA, BizmiwA, BizmizwA, BizmikA, dagDikA. — (Fried rice) DAnAH f. pl., DAnAkAH f. pl.; ‘the meal of it,’ DAnAcUrRaM. — (Rice flattened by threshing) DAnyacamasaH, pfTukaH -kaM. — (Oblation of rice) arGaH, arGyaM, caruH m. — (Heap of rice for presentation) DAnyaDenuH f., DAnyAcalaH, taRqulOGaH. — (Rice-water) taRqulodakaM, taRqulAmbu n., taRqurIRaH. — (Rice-gruel) yavAgUH f., uzRikA, SrARA, vilepI, taralA, DAnyAmlaM. — (Rice-field) SAlikzetraM. — (Rice-milk) pAyasaH -saM. — (Rice-husk) tuzaH. — (Ear of rice) kaRiSaH -SaM, DAnyaSIrzakaM. — (Granary for rice) kuSUlaH, vrIhyagAraM. — (Having rice, bearing it, made of it) vrIhimayaH -yI -yaM, vrIhikaH -kA -kaM, vrIhI -hiRI -hi (n), vrEhaH -hI -haM, vrEheyaH -yI -yaM, SAleyaH -yI -yaM, SAlimayaH &c.

Rich, m. Dana-vitta-dravya-vat, Danin, Dana-vitta-SAlin, saDana, mahA-bahu-Dana, arTavat, Danika, DanAQya, viBavasaMpanna, DanasamfdDa, SrImat, lakzmIvat; samfdDa, DaneSvara, lakzmISa; saMpannavat, SAlin, yukta in comp. with Wealth, q. v. 2 (Costly) mahArha-rGa, bahumUlya, mahAmUlya, atipratApavat. 3 AQya, bahula, pracura, pUrRa, bahu, samfdDa, saMpanna, maya in comp.; ‘r(ich) perfume’ bahalAmodaH; ‘r(ich) in beauty’ rUpAQya; guRAQya, bahula-ratna, &c. 4 satva-sArasattva-sAra-guRa-vat, sPIta, bahuPalaprada, urvarA (BUmiH), sasyAQya. 5 ujjvala, suprakASa, atiSoBana (colours). 6 Gfta-pluta-pUrRa. [Rich]es, s. DanaM, arTaH, viBavaH, vittaM, dravyaM; See Wealth. 2 DanAQyatA, saDanatA, DanabAhulyaM. [Rich]ly, adv. bahuDanena, praBUtaM, BUri, mahAmUlyena, atiSoBayA, ati-pratApena, saSrIkaM; ‘r(ichly) decorated’ atiSoBayA prasADita, saviSezamaMqita. [Rich]ness, s. DanAQyatA, saSrIkatA, saDanatA, sPItatA, mahArGatA, atiSoBA, pratApaH; bAhulyaM, samfdDi f., saMpad f.; ‘r(ichness) of beauty’ rUpa-saMpad, lAvaRyAtiSayaH; ‘r(ichness) of expression’ vacasAmudAratA (Mal. 1).

RICH: I Wealthy:(1) Danin (f. nI), if we are r. with wealth undistributed and unenjoyed: dAnopaBogahInena Danena Danino yadi, H. i. 156.;(2) Danavat (f. tI);(3) DanaSAlin (f. nI);(4) mahADana (f. nA), DanAQya (f. QyA), and sim. comp.s. (= very r.);(5) vittaSAlin (f. nI); (6) viBavasampanna (f. nnA);(7) by subs., he has friends, who is r.: yasyArTAstasya mitrARi, H. i. 124.II Costly, splendid; q. v.: mahADana (f. nA) and sim. comp. s, r. couch: mahADanaM Sayanam, Ki. i. 38.III Abundant: q. v.: pracura (f. rA).IV Abounding in:(1) AQya (f. QyA), a fort r. in weapons and machines: durgamAyuDayantrAQyam, Ka. iv. 60.;(2) by words given under abundant, the first became r. in gems: praTamA bahuratnasUraBUt. R. viii. 28.;(3) samanvita (f. tA = endowed with: q. v.), r. in ore: KanidravyasamanvitA, Ka. iv. 51.: v. Also having. V. Of soil etc.:(1) sAravat or guRavat (f. tI), Ka. iv. 50. and ix. 18.;(2) praSasta (f. stA): v. Excellent.VI Of colours: ujjvala (f. lA = bright).VII Highly sea- -soned:(1) Gftapluta (f. tA) and sim. comp.s. (= full of ghee);(2) sumaDura (f. rA = very sweet), Bha.

RICH , a. (Wealthy) DanI -ninI -ni (n), DanavAn -vatI -vat (t), saDanaH -nA -naM, mahADanaH -nA -naM, bahuDanaH &c., vittavAn &c., vasumAn &c., arTavAn &c., arTAnvitaH -tA -taM, sArTaH -rTA -rTaM, DanasampannaH -nnA -nnaM, DanikaH -kA -kaM, DanAQyaH -QyA -QyaM, DanasamfdDaH -dDA -dDaM, Danavi- pulaH -lA -laM, lakzmIvAn &c., SrImAn &c., saSrIkaH -kA -kaM, koza- vAn &c., sampattimAn &c., samfdDaH &c., DaneSvaraH &c., lakzmISaH, iByaH -ByA -ByaM; ‘extremely rich person,’ atiDanI &c., lakzADISaH, kowISvaraH, kowyaDISaH, lakzapatiH m., kuveraH. — (Abounding in) AQyaH -QyA -QyaM, pUrRa in comp., bahu in comp., bahula in comp., pracura in comp., sampanna in comp., samfdDa in comp., puzkala in comp., maya in comp., aDika in comp.; ‘rich in good qualities,’ guRAQyaH &c., guRasampannaH -nnA -nnaM. — (Fertile) sPItaH -tA -taM, pInaH -nA -naM, bahuPaladaH -dA -daM. — (Costly, splendid) mahArGaH -rGA -rGaM, mahA- mUlyaH -lyA -lyaM, bahumUlyaH &c., atiSoBanaH -nA -naM, atiSoBAnvitaH -tA -taM, tEjasaH -sI -saM, atitEjasaH &c., pratApavAn &c. — (As a dish) GftapUrRaH -rRA -rRaM, GftaplutaH -tA -taM, GftamayaH -yI -yaM.
RICHES: (1) Danam, every one is strong with r.: DanavAn balavAn sarvaH, H. i. 121.: v. Money, wealth;(2) samfdDiH: v. Opulence.

RICHES , s. DanaM, vittaM, vasu n., arTaH, sampattiH f., dravyaM, viBavaH, lakzmIH f., SrIH f., rAH m. (rE), sampad f. — (State of having great riches) DanAQyatA, DanabAhulyaM, DanaprAcuryyaM, DanasamfdDiH f., DanavEpulyaM, DanESvaryyaM, DanasampattiH f., mahADanatvaM, saDanatA; ‘desirous of riches,’ DanArTI -rTinI -rTi (n); ‘desire of riches,’ DanASA, DanatfzRA; ‘pride of riches,’ DanadarpaH; ‘puffed up by riches,’ DanagarvitaH -tA -taM.
RICHLY: I With riches: praBUtaDanena and sim. comp.s.II Sumptuously, splendidly: q. v.: expr. by adj.III Plentifully, exceedingly: q. v.: BUri.

RICHLY , adv. (With riches) saDanaM, DanabAhulyena, bahuDanena, mahADanena. — (Splendidly) mahAmUlyena, atiSoBayA, atiSoBApUrvvaM. — (Abundantly) bAhulyena, atibahulaM, prAcuryyeRa, vEpulyena, vipulaM, ativipulaM, samfdDA.

RICHNESS: I Lit.: DanAQyatA and sim. comp.s. II Costliness: mahADanatA and sim. comp.s. III Abundance: q. v.: prAcuryam.IV Of soil: sAra- or guRavattA.V Excellence: q. v.: praSastatA.VI Of colours: ujjvalatA.VII Of dishes: sumaDuratA.

RICHNESS , s. (Opulence) DanAQyatA, saDanatA, DanabAhulyaM, DanasamfdDiH f., DanasampattiH f., DanikatA, saSrIkatA, see RICHES. — (Fertility) sPItatA, pInatA, sPItiH f., bahuPalatA. — (Costliness, splendor) mahArGatA, mahAmUlyatA, SoBA, atiSoBA, tejas n., pratApaH. — (Abun dance) bAhulyaM, prAcuryyaM, vEpulyaM, samfdDiH f., samfdDatA. — (Of a dish) GftapUrRatA, mizwatA.
Rick, s. (Of corn or hay) rASiH, saMcayaH.
RICK: rASiH: v. Heap, stock.
RICK , s. (Stack) citiH f., cayaH, utkaraH, rASiH m., nicayaH, nikaraH oGaH; ‘of hay,’ tfRotkaraH, tfRacitiH f., see HAY-RICK.
Rickets, s. bAlagrahaH.
RICKETS: a disease: bAlagrahaH (gen.), Bha.
RICKETS , s. pl. bAlarogaH, bAlavyADiH m., bAlAmayaH.
Rickety, a. SiTilasaMDi, asTira, adfQa-saMDi; (building) jIrRa, jarjarita.
RICKETY: I Lit.: grahajuzwa (f. zwA).II Shaky: SiTilasanDi (mfn.) and sim. comp.s.
RICKETY , a. SiTilasanDiH -nDiH -nDi; adfQasanDiH &c., asTiraH -rA -raM, anavasTitaH -tA -taM, vicalaH -lA -laM, calasvaBAvaH -vA -vaM, sKali- tagatiH -tiH -ti.

Rid, v. t. muc 6 P or c., mokz 10, vi-, SuD c., ud-hf 1 P; ‘to get r(id) of’ apa-nI 1 P, nirAkf, tyaj 1 P, apa-hA 3 P, niH-sf c., apAs 4 U; oft. by nir pr.; ‘r(id) of thorns’ nizkaMwakIkf; ‘r(id) of difficulties’ nirviGnIkf. a. vi-, mukta, varjita, hIna, rahita, gata, vIta, hfta, nir, a in comp.; kaMwakahIna, niHSalya, &c. [Rid]dance, s. mukti f., mokzaH, udDAraH, SoDanaM.
RID: muYcati or mocayati vi-, (muc, c. 6. and 10.) : v. To free, deliver. To get r. of: niHsArayati (c. of sf): v. To remove, drive away.

To RID , v. a. (Free from encumbrance, &c.) viGnAt or mArAd muc (c. 6. muYcati, moktuM) or SuD (c. 10. SoDayati -yituM) or viSuD or udDf (c. 1. -harati -harttuM) or mokz (c. 10. mokzayati -yituM), viGnaM or BAram apanI or vinI or hf, nirviGnIkf; ‘to rid of thieves,’ kaRwakAn udDf, kaRwakodDaraRaM kf, kaRwakaSoDanaM kf, nizkaRwakIkf; ‘of thorns,’ SalyodDAraM kf, SalpAni udDf.

RID , a. muktaH -ktA -ktaM, vimuktaH &c., SoDitaH -tA -taM, varjitaH &c., rahitaH &c., vigata in comp., vIta in comp., gata in comp., hIna in comp., hfta in comp., nir or a prefixed; ‘rid of thieves or thorns,’ kaRwakamuktaH -ktA -ktaM, muktakaRwakaH -kA -kaM, vigatakaRwakaH &c., vItakaRwakaH &c., kaRwakahInaH -nA -naM, hftakaRwakaH &c., nizka- RwakaH &c., ‘to be rid of,’ Buc in pass. (mucyate), vimuc; ‘to get rid of,’ apAs, niras, nirAkf, tyaj, parityaj, apasfj, apahA, see To DISCARD; ‘to be got rid of,’ tyAjyaH -jyA -jyaM, apAsa- nIyaH -yA -yaM, nirAkaraRIyaH &c.
RIDDANCE: muktiH: v. Deliverance, escape.
RIDDANCE , s. muktiH f., mocanaM, muktatA, mokzaH -kzaRaM, udDAraH, udDaraRaM, SoDanaM, SudDiH f., nistAraH, trARaM, paritrARaM.
Riddle, s. prahelikA, pravahlikA, paSnadUtI; gUQaM, kUwapraSnaH. 2 SoDanI, cAlanI. v. t. SuD c. 2 vyaD 4 P; See Perforate.
RIDDLE (subs.): I Enigma:(1) prahelikA; (2) pravahRiH, kA.II A sieve: q. v.: SoDanI.

RIDDLE (v.): I To clean grass: SoDayati, vi-, (c. of SuD), D. vi.II To pierce: q. v.: viDyati (vyaD, c. 4.).III To speak enig- -matically: prahelikAM vadati (vad, c. l.): v. To say, tell.IV To un-r.: q. v.

RIDDLE , s. pravahliH f. -hlikA, prahelikA, praSnadUtI, kUwapraSnaH, dfzwakUwaM gUQapraSnaH, gUQaM, gUQavAkyaM, SlezaH, SlezoktiH f.; different kinds are sarvvatoBadraH, vardDamAnaH, antarlApikA, vahirlApikA. — (Large sieve) SoDanI, vfhaccAlanI, mahAcAlanI.
To RIDDLE , v. a. (Clean grain) pUrvvoktayantreRa SuD (c. 10. SoDayati -yituM), or SoDanaM kf or utpavanaM kf. — (Perforate) vyaD, Cidr, CidrapUrRaM -rRAM kf, saCidrIkf.

Ride, v. i. aSvena saMcar 1 A or gam 1 P or yA 2 P or cal 1 P, aSvena &c. vah pass. v. t. (aSvaM &c.) A-aDi-samA-aDyA-ruh 1 P, aDyA-A-kram 1 U, 4 P, aDi-zWA 1 P, aDyAs 2 A. s. aSvena saMcaraRaM or viharaRaM. [Rid]er, s. aSvArohaH, aSvaArohin m., aSvArUQaH. 2 Arohin m., ArUQaH. [Rid]ing, s. aSvArohaRaM. a. ArUQa, Arohin, Aroha, ASrayin in comp.

RIDE (v.): (1) A- rohati, aDi-, samaDi-, samA-, aDyA-, (ruh, c. l.), rose in order to r.: Arurukzuruda- tizWat, K. ; r. ing on it: samAruhya tam, K. ; r. for the battle on a great marine monster: yudDe'DirUQaH makaraM mahattaram, Ku. xiv. 9.;(2) aDitizWati (sTA, c. l. = be seated on), r. ing in their excellent vehicles: svavAhanAni pravarARyaDizWitAH, Ku. xiv. 13.
RIDE (subs.): I The act: to take a r.: aSvena saYcarate (car, c. l.) or viharati (hf, c. l.): v. Also R. ing.II A road: perh. vITiH, M. n.

To RIDE , v. n. (Be carried on horseback) aSvana vah in pass. (uhyate), aSvena saYcar (c. 1. -carati -rituM) or car, aSvena gam (c. 1. gacCati, gantuM) or yA (c. 2. yAti -tuM), aSvavAhanena gam or yA or cal. — (On an elephant) gajena vah in pass. or saYcar or gam or yA or cal, gajavAhanena cal or vraj. — (Be borne on a fluid, &c.) vah in pass., plu (c. 1. plavate, plotuM).

To RIDE , v. a. (Sit on a horse) aSvam Aruh (c. 1. -rohati -roQuM) or aDiruh or aDyAruh or samAruh or aDikram (c. 1. -krAmati -kramituM), aSvArUQaH -QA -QaM BU, aSvArohI -hiRI -hi BU, aSvArohaRaM kf. — (Sit on an elephant) gajArUQaH -QA -QaM BU, gajArohI &c. BU, gajam Aruh. — (On the back of a peacock) mayUrapfzWArUQaH -QA -QaM BU, mayUrapfzWam Aruh or ASri. — (A chariot) yAnArUQaH -QA -QaM BU, yAnam Aruh, yAnArohaRaM kf.
RIDE , s. aSvena gamanaM or calanaM, aSvena viharaRaM, aSvArohaRaM ‘to take a ride,’ aSvena vihAraM kf or vihf, aSvena BramaRaM ka or pariBramaRaM kf.
RIDER: I Horse-r.:(1) aSvArohin (f. RI); (2) aSvArUQa (f. QA); and sim. comp.s.II In gen.: Arohin (f. RI): v. To ride.III An addition: perh. sahayogaH.
RIDER , s. (On a horse) aSvArohI m. (n), aSvAroQA m. (Qf), aSvArUQaH, see HORSE-MAN. — (In general) AroQA m., ArohI m., rohakaH
Ridge, s. kawakaH-kaM, utsaMgaH. 2 pfzWaM. 3 setuH, DaraRaH, Ali f., piMqalaH. [Ridg]y, a. sakawaka.
RIDGE: no prop. equiv.: (1) pfzWam (= back); (2) kawaka (mn. = side of a hill);(3) SreRiH, (RI = chain).
RIDGE , s. (Of a mountain) kawakaH -kaM, kUwaM, dantaH, ucCrAyaH. — (Of earth, a mound) setuH m., piRqalaH, piRqilaH, DaraRaH, AliH -lI f., saMvaraH, jaNgAlaH. — (Back, top) pfzWaM, agraM
RIDGY , a. sakawakaH -kA -kaM, kawakAkAraH -rA -raM, kawakarUpaH -pA -paM.

Ridicule, v. t. upa-ava-has 1 P, upahA-syatAM nI 1 P, upahAsAspadaM kf 8 U, avahAsAspadIkf, A-ava-kzip 6 P; See Contemn, also; ‘I shall be r(idicul)ed’ gamizyAmyupahAsyatAM (R. i. 3); ‘to be r(idicul)ed’ upahAsyatAM gam 1 P or yA 2 P. s. upa-ava-hAsaH-hasanaM, A-ava-kzepaH, avajYA, avahelanA, upahAsyatA. [Ridicul]ous, a. ava-upa-hAsya, hAsAspadIBUta, hAsayogya, upahAsArha, hAsAspadaM, hAsakara (rI f.), hAsotpAdaka.
RIDICULE (subs.): upahAsaH or avahAsaH or apahAsaH, I shall merit r.: gamizyAmyupahAsyatAm, R. i. 3. : v. Also contempt.
RIDICULE (v.): upa- hasati, ava-, apa-, (has, c. 1.), either I shall be r. d by good men: apahasye'TavA sadBiH, Ki. xi. 68.: v. Also to laugh.

RIDICULE , s. upahAsaH, parihAsaH, apahAsaH, avahAsaH prahAsaH, prahasanaM, upahasanaM, upahasitaM, upahasanIyatA, vihasitaM, hasanaM, hAsya, hAmikA. pariBAzaRaM, avakzepaH, avahelA, avajYA, utprAsanaM, utsmaya, -yanaM.

To RIDICULE , v. a. upahas (c. 1. -hasati -situM), avahas, apahas, upahA- saBUmiM kf, avahAsaBUmiM kf, avahAsAppadaM kf, avahAsAspadIkf, apahA- sAspadIkf, hAspAspadIkf, avahAsasTAnaM kf, utsmi (c. 1. -smayate -smetuM) [Page692-a+ 51] aBismi, avakziy, Akzip. See To DERIDE.
RIDICULED , p. p. upahasitaH -tA -taM, avahasitaH &c., AkziptaH -ptA -ptaM.
RIDICULOUS: upa-, apa-, or ava- hAsya (f. syA) : v. Also contemptible.

RIDICULOUS , a. upahAsyaH -syA -syaM, avahAsyaH &c., parihAsyaH &c., hAsyaH &c., hAsyajanakaH -kA -kaM, hAsajanakaH, hAsakaraH -rI -raM. hAsyotpAdakaH &c., hAsotpAdakaH &c., upahAsayogyaH -gyA -gyaM, upahA- sArhaH -rhA -rhaM, upahAsavizayaH -yA -yaM, hAsyAspadaH -dA -daM, takyaH -kyA -kyaM.
RIDICULOUSLY , adv. hAsyaprakAreRa, upahAsyaprakAreRa, upahAsyaM.
RIDICULOUSNESS: upa-, apa- or ava-hAsyatA.
RIDICULOUSNESS , s. upahAsyatA, apahAsyatA, parihAsyatA, hAsyatvaM.

RIDING: (subs.): I The act: aSvArohaRam and sim. comp. s., skill in r.: turaNgArohaRapAwavam, D.; r. -habit: turaNgADirohaRocito vezaH, K. : v. Horse, to ride.II Of a country: *maRqalaKaRqaH; pramaRqalam.
RIDING , s. aSvArohaRaM, hayArohaH, aSvArohaRavidyA, aSvavidyA.

RIDING , part. ArohI -hiRI -hi (n), ArUQaH -QA -QaM, Aroha in comp., rohaka in comp., ASrayI &c.; ‘riding on a horse,’ aSvArohI &c.; ‘on an elephant,’ gajArUQaH &c.; ‘on the back of a peacock,’ mayUrapfzWArUQaH &c., mayUrapfzWASrayI &c.
RIDING-SCHOOL , s. aSvArohaRaSAlA, aSvaSikzASAlA, hayaSikzASAlA.
Rife, a. sarvatra pracalita, pravftta, pracala, bahula.
RIFE (adj.): pracala (f. lA): v. Prevalent.
RIFE , a. prasidDaH -dDA -dDaM, pracalaH -lA -laM. See PREVALENT.
RIFENESS , s. prasidDatA, prasidDiH f., bAhulyaM. See PREVALENCE.
RIFF-RAFF , s. KalAH m. pl., pfTagjanAH, aDamavarRAH &c. See RABBLE.
Riff-raff, s. aDamAH, prAkfta-pfTag-janAH.
Rifle, s. AgneyAstraM. v. t. apa-hf 1 P; See Rob.
RIFLE: I Subs.: AgneyAstram.II Verb: harati (hf, c. 1.): v. To rob.
To RIFLE , v. a. hf (c. 1. harati, harttuM), apahf, aBihf. See To ROB.
RIFLE , s. (Kind of gun) sItArUpeRa suzirIkftA gulikAprakzepaRI.
RIFLEMAN: AgneyAstraBft (mfn.), -DArin (f. RI), etc.
RIFT: Cidram: v. Crack, cleft.
RIFT , s. CidraM, BittiH f., BaNgaH. See CLEFT, FISSURE.
To RIFT , v. a. Bid, viBid, Cid. See To CLEAVE, SPLIT.
Rig, v. t. sajjIkf 8 U, upakaraREH upakxp c. 2 See Frolic. [Rig]ging, sajjA, sAmagrI, paricCadaH, rajjvAdisADanaM, potasajjA.
RIG (v.): sajjate (sajj, c. 1.): v. To equip.
RIG, RIGGING (subs.): (1) sajjA (= equip- -ment);(2) rajjavaH (= ropes: of ship's r.).
To RIG , v. a. sajjIkf, sajj (c. 1. sajjati -jjituM), sasajjaM -jjAM kf. — (A ship) nAvaM samudrayAnArTaM vAtavasanAdinA sajjIkf or samAyuj. See To EQUIP.
RIG , RIGGING, s. sajjA, sajjanaM -nA, nOkAsajjA -jjanaM, vAtavasanAdi- sajjA, rajjvAdisajjanaM, vasanarajjvAdi, vasanaM, paricCadaH.
RIGGED , p. p. sajjIkftaH -tA -taM, sajjitaH &c., vasanarajjvAdiyuktaH &c.

Right, a. dakziRa, vAmetara, savyetara, apasavya; ‘to the r(ight)’ dakziRataH, dakziRena; ‘r(ight) hand’ agrahastaH-karaH, dakziRapARiH. 2 ucita, nyAyya, yukta, upapanna, samyac, yaTAnyAya, Darmya, sADu, samaMjasa, sat-su in comp.; ‘r(ight) path’ sanmArgaH, supaTaH. 3 satya, yaTArTa, avitaTa, taTya; See True; ‘Priyamvada is r(ight)’ or ‘says r(ight)ly’ avitaTamAha priyaMvadA (S. 1); ‘you are r(ight)’ satyaM-yaTArTaM-Aha-BavAn. 4 sarala, fju, avakra; ‘r(ight) angle’ samakoRaH, fjukoRaH. s. dakziRapArSvaH-dik; dakziRaH, apasavyaM; ‘on the r(ight)’ dakziRataH, dakziRasyAM viSi. 2 nyAyaH, DarmaH, nyAyyatA, nyAyitA, OcityaM, yATArTyaM, nIti f., yuktatA. 3 satyatA, taTyatA, SudDatA. 4 aDikAraH, svatvaM, svAmyaM, sattA; oft. ex. by arh 1 P; ‘a woman has no r(ight) to independence’ na strI svAtaMtryamarhati. adv. yuktaM, nyAyataH, sTAne, sADu, ucitaM, yaTocitaM, yaTAnyAyaM, upapannaM, samyak; ‘I acted r(ight) in delivering her into the charge of the queen’ enAM devIhaste nikzipatA mayA yuktamevAnuzWitaM (Rat. 1). 2 satyaM, yaTArTaM, saralaM, fju; su-ati pr. interj. sADu, yuktaM, BadraM, bAQaM. v. t. fjUkf 8 U, susTIkf, samA-pratisamA-DA 3 U. v. i. sarala-fju a. BU 1 P. [Right]eous, a. nyAyaparAyaRa-para, sADuvftta, pavitra, nyAyAcAra, suSIla; (of acts) nyAyya, yukta; See Just. [Right]eously, adv. nyAyataH, DarmeRa. [Right]eousness, s. sadAcAraH, sADuvfttaM. [Right]ful, a. aDikArin, svatvaviSizwa. 2 Just, q. v. [Right]fully, adv. sADikAraM. [Right]ly, adv. ucitaM, satyaM, yaTArTataH, paramArTataH, yaTArTaM, sTAne, yuktaM, yaTADarmaM, yaTAnyAyaM, nyAyataH, samyak. 2 satyaM; See Truly.

RIGHT (adj.): I Not left:(1) dakziRa (f. RA), on the r.: dakziRataH; wounded on the r.: dakziRerman (mfn.), B. iv. 44.;(2) vAmetara or savyetara (f. rA: poet.), by the r. eye: savyetareRAkzRA, R. xiv. 49.;(3) apasavya (f. vyA: rare).II Straight: q. v.: r. line: saralareKA; r. angle: samakoRaH. III Proper; reasonable: q. v.:(1) ucita (f. tA), sam-;(2) nyAyya, (f. yyA).IV Real, actual: q. v.: yaTArTa (f. rTA).V True, correct: q. v.: satya (f. tyA).

RIGHT (subs.): I Justice, propriety: q. v.: DarmaH.II Just claim, title:(1) aDikAraH; (2) svatvam.III. R. side: v. Right. (adj. 1.). IV What is r.: expr. by adj., neither I did r. to him: etasminnucitaM na nAma vihitam, Vi. v. 46.; you are in the r.: satye tvaM vartase (?).
RIGHT (v.): I Lit.:(1) fjUkaroti;(2) samI- karoti.II To do r. to: ucitaM vidaDAti (DA, c. 3.), vyavaharati (hf, c. 1.), etc.

RIGHT , a. (Just, fit, proper) yuktaH -ktA -ktaM, upayuktaH &c., yaTAyuktaH &c., yaTAyogyaH -gyA -gyaM, samyaN samIcI samyak, samaYjasaH -sA -saM, yogyaH &c., nyAyyaH -yyA -yyaM, ucitaH -tA -taM, yaTocitaH &c., samI- cInaH -nA -naM, yaTArTaH -rTA -rTaM, yATArTikaH -kI -kaM, samucitaH &c., sADuH -DuH -DvI -Du, laByaH -ByA -ByaM, see PROFER. — (True, correct) ftaH -tA -taM, satyaH -tyA -tya, taTyaH -TyA -TyaM, avitaTaH -TA -TaM, yaTArTaH &c., SudDaH -dDA -dDaM. — (Straight) saralaH -lA -laM, fjuH -juH -ju, ajihmaH -hmA -hmaM; ‘a right line,’ saralareKA. — (Not left) dakziRaH -RA -RaM, apasavyaH -vyA -vyaM, avasavya &c., vAmetaraH -rA -raM; ‘right and left,’ savyApasavyaH -vyA -vyaM; ‘to the right,’ pradakziRaH -RA -RaM; ‘winding to the right,’ dakziRAbarttI -rttinI -rtti (n); ‘the right side,’ see RIGHT, s.; ‘the right hand,’ dakziRapARiH m., agrapARiH m., agrahastaH, agrakaraH; ‘being on the right hand,’ dakziRasTaH -sTA -sTaM; ‘right ascension, in astronomy,’ vizuvAMSaH.

RIGHT , s. (Justice, propriety) DarmmaH, nyAyaH, nItiH f., nyAyyatvaM -tA, nyAyitA, nyAyatA, yuktiH f., yuktatA, yogyatA, upayuktatA, upayogitA, yaTAyogyatA, yaTArTatA, yATArTyaM, sAmaYjasyaM, samyaktvaM, OcityaM, ucitatvaM, samaYjasaM; ‘right and wrong,’ DarmmADarmmaM, yuktAyuktaM, nyAyAnyAyaM, hi- tAhitaM. — (Correctness) satyatA, satyaM, ftaM, avitaTaM, samaYjasaM, SudDatA. — (Just claim, title) aDikAraH -ritvaM, svatvaM, svAmyaM, sattA; ‘to have a right,’ arh (c. 1. arhati -rhituM); ‘a woman has no right to independence,’ strI na svAtantryam arhati. — (The right side, not the left) dakziRaM, apasavyaM, avasavyaM, vAmetaraM, dakziRadik f. (S), dakziRapArSvaH, dakziRANgaM; ‘right and left,’ savyApasavyaM; ‘upon [Page692-b+ 51] the right side,’ dakziRasTaH -sTA -sTaM; ‘on the right,’ dakziRa- pArSve, dakziRatas, dakziRena. — (One's own right) svADikAraH, svasvatvaM, ‘to set to rights,’ see To RIGHT, v. a.

RIGHT , adv. (Justly) yuktaM, yaTAyuktaM, yaTAyogyaM, yaTocitaM, yaTAnyAyaM, Darmmatas, nyAyatas, samaYjasaM, samyak, yaTArTaM, sTAne. — (Truly) satyaM, ftaM, aYjasA, arTatas, yaTArTatas. — (In a straight line) saralaM, fju, ajihmaM, avakraM. — (To a great degree) su or ati prefixed.
RIGHT , interj. sADu, BadraM, yuktaM, svasti, vAQaM.

To RIGHT , v. a. (Restore to a right position, set to rights) susTa (nom. susTayati -yituM), susTaM -sTAM kf, svasTa (nom. svasTayati -yituM), svasTaM -sTAM kf, see To RESTORE, v. a. — (Do justice to) nyAyaM kf.
To RIGHT , v. n. (Become right) susTaH -sTA -sTaM BU, svasTaH -sTA -sTaM BU. — (Become erect) fjuH -juH -ju BU, fjUBU.
RIGHT-ANGLE , s. samakoRaH, samalambaH, samalambakoRaH, samalambadviBujaH.
RIGHT-ANGLED: (1) samakoRa (f. RA);(2) fju- koRa (f. RA).
RIGHT-HAND , s. dakziRapARiH m., dakziRahastaH, dakziRakaraH, agrahastaH, see RIGHT, a.
RIGHT-HANDED , a. dakziRahastasevI -vinI -vi (n), dakziRasAcI &c.
RIGHT-MINDED: SudDacetas (mfn.) and sim. comp. s.: v. Honest.
RIGHTEOUS: I Just, proper: q. v.: nyAyya (f. yyA).II Virtuous, holy: q. v.: nyAya- parAyaRa (f. RA).
RIGHTEOUS , a. DArmmikaH -kI -kaM, nyAyAcAraH -rA -raM, nyAyAcArI -riRI &c., nyAyaparaH -rA -raM, puRyaH -RyA -RyaM, sADuH -DuH -DvI -Du, DarmmavarttI &c. See JUST.
RIGHTEOUSLY: (1) nyAyataH (= justly);(2) by adj. or circumlo.
RIGHTEOUSLY , adv. Darmmatas, nyAyatas, DarmmAnusAreRa. See JUSTLY.
RIGHTEOUSNESS: (1) nyAyyatA (of acts);(2) nyAyaparAyaRatA (of men): v. Piety, rectitude, purity, propriety.
RIGHTEOUSNESS , s. DarmmaH, DarmmatA, DArmmikatA -tvaM, nyAyaH, nyAyyatA, nyAyitA, sADutA -tvaM, puRyatA, SucitA. See JUSTICE.
RIGHTFUL: nyAyya (f. yyA): v. Lawful, just.
RIGHTFUL , a. (Having a just title) aDikArI -riRI -ri (n), aDi- kAravAn -vatI -vat (t), sADikAraH -rA -raM, svatvADikArI &c. — (Agreeable to justice), see JUST.
RIGHTFULLY: nyAyena: v. Lawfully, justly.
RIGHTFULLY , adv. aDikAreRa, aDikAratas, sADikAraM. See JUSTLY.
RIGHTFULNESS , s. aDikAritA, aDikAravattvaM, sADikAratvaM, see JUSTICE.
RIGHTLY: I Properly, fitly: q. v.: ucitam. II Truly, correctly: q. v.: yaTArTataH, r. called “distresser of foes”: parantapo nAma yaTArTanAmA, R. vi. 21.III Well: q. v.: samyak.

RIGHTLY , adv. yuktaM, samyak, Darmmatas, DarmmeRa, nyAyatas, yaTAnyAyaM, yaTA- yogyaM, yaTADarmmaM, yaTArTaM, yaTocitaM, samaYjasaM, sTAne, see JUSTLY, FITLY. — (Truly) satyaM, ftaM, aYjasA, yaTArTaM -rTatas, see TRULY.
RIGHTNESS , s. yaTArTatA, yATArTyaM, satyatA, sAmaYjasyaM, samyaktvaM, SudDatA.

Rigid, a. kaWora, karkaSa, ugra, dAruRa, paruza. 2 dfQa, Gana, kaWina, aSiTila, amfdu. [Rigid]ity, [Rigid]ness, s. kaWoratA, kaWinatA, dfQatA, GanatA, kAWinyaM. [Rigid]ly, adv. dfQaM, kaWinaM, aSiTilaM; See Strict.
RIGID: kaWora (f. rA): v. Stern, severe, hard.

RIGID , a. (Stiff, not pliant) dfQaH -QA -QaM, stabDaH -bDA -bDaM, stabDIkftaH -tA -taM, GanaH -nA -naM, kaWinaH -nA -naM, stimitaH -tA -taM, aSiTilaH -lA -laM, amfduH -duH -dvI -du. — (Strict, severe) kaWoraH -rA -raM, karkaSaH -SA -SaM, ugraH -grA -graM, niyataH -tA -taM, sUkzmaH -kzmA -kzmaM, sUkzmadarSI &c.
RIGIDITY: kaWoratA: v. Stiffness, hardness.
RIGIDITY , RIGIDNESS, s. dfQatA, stabDatA, GanatA, kaWinatA, kAWinyaM, dArQyaM, kaWoratA, karkaSatA, kArkaSyaM, ugratA -tvaM, aSiTilatA, aSETilyaM; ‘of the eye-lids,’ vartmAvabanDaH
RIGIDLY: kaWoram: v. Stiffly, hardly.
RIGIDLY , adv. dfQaM, sudfQaM, stabDaM, stabDatayA, stabDatvena, sagrAWinyaM, sadArQyaM, sakArkaSyaM, kaWoraM, kaWinaM aSiTilaM.
Rigmarole, s. anarTakakaTA.
RIGMAROLE: gUQapralapitam, and sim. comp. s.
RIGMAROLE , s. anarTakakaTA, niraTakakaTA, asambadDArTakA dIrGakaTA.
RIGOR, RIGOUR: I In gen.: kaWoratA: v. Stiffness, hardness.II Intensity, severity: q. v.: ugratA.
RIGOR , s. (Stiffness) dfQatA, kaWinatA, kaWoratA, kAWinyaM, see RI- GIDITY. — (Severity) ugratA, ugradaRqatA -tvaM, kaWoratA, karkaSatA, nizWu- ratA, nEzWuryyaM. — (Intensity) see the word.
RIGOROUS: kaWora (f. rA), r. imprisonment: kaWora- niroDaH: v. Stiff, hard, severe.

RIGOROUS , a. (Severe) ugradaRqaH -RqA -RqaM, ugraH -grA -graM udyatadaRqaH &c., kaWoraH -rA -raM, nizWuraH -rA -raM, kaWinaH -nA -naM, krUraH &c., karkaSaH -SA -SaM. — (Exact) sUkzmaH -kzmA -kzmaM. — See STRICT.
RIGOROUSLY , adv. ugratvena, ugraM, ugradaRqena, kaWoraM, nizWuraM, nEzWuryyeRa

Rigour, s. dfQatA, kAWinyaM, aSETilyaM. 2 ugratA, kaWoratA, karkaSatA, nizWuratA. [Rigour]ous, a. kaWora, nizWura, ugra, paruza, tIzRadaMqatIkzRadaMqa, asO-mya, karkaSa, kaWina. 2 sUkzma; See Strict. [Rigour]ously, adv. ugraM, nizWuraM, paruzaM.
Rile, v. t. kzuB c., kup c.
Rill, s. kusarit f., kzudranadI, kulyA.
RILL: (1) kusarit (f.), H. ;(2) kzudranadI; and sim. comp. s.
RILL , s. alpanadI, kzudranadI, alpasarit f., sUkzmasarit, kzudrasarit f.
Rim, s. prAMtaH, aMtaH, DArA, karRaH (of ships).
RIM: (1) prAntaH: v. Border, edge;(2) karRaH (of vessels).
RIM , s. prAntaH, antaH, DAraH -rA, prAntaBAgaH, antaBAgaH, utsaNgaH, pArSvaH; ‘of a cup,’ pAtraprAntaH, pAtrakaRWaH, pAtrapArSvaH.
RIME: GananIhAraH: v. Hoar-frost.
RIME , s. tuzAraH, nIhAraH, kujJawiH f. -wikA. See HOAR-FROST.
RIMY: atihima (f. mA) and sim. comp. s.: v. Frosty, frost.
RIMY , a. tuzAramayaH -yI -yaM, nIhAramayaH &c., kujJawikAmayaH &c.
Rind, s. tvac f., valkaH-lkaM, valkalaH-laM, SalkaM, carman n., kaMcukaH.
RIND: (1) tvac (f.): v. Bark, skin;(2) kaYcukaH (= coat, shell).

RIND , s. tvak f. (c), tvacA, valkaM -lkalaM, SalkaM -lkalaM, carmma n. (n), CalliH -llI f., SallakaM, cocaM -cakaM, colakaM, cIraM, aRqakozaH; ‘having rind,’ tvacIyAn -yasI -yaH (s), tvacizWaH -zWA -zWaM.

Ring, v. i. raR-kvaR 1 P, vi-ru 2 P, SiMj 2 A. v. t. cal c., vad c., Ahan 2 U. nad c., kvaR c., ‘r(ing) the bell’ GaMwAM vAdaya, GaMwAnAdaM kuru. s. aMgulI(rI)yaM-yakaM, UrmikA; ‘signet r(ing)’ aMgulimudrA, mudrA. 2 valayaH-yaM, maMqalaM, cakraM; ‘dancing in a r(ing)’ maMqalanftyaM. 3 maMqalaM (of persons). 4 raMgaH. 5 SiMjitaM, kvaRitaM, kvaRanaM, ni-, kvA(kva)RaH, ravaH, nAdaH; ‘r(ing)-leader’ nAyakaH, agraRIH, muKyaH, pravartakaH, muKaraH, praDAnarAja-drohin m. (of conspirators); ‘r(ing) worm’ dadrumaMqalaM, maMqalakuzWaM; ‘having r(ing)worm’ dadru(drU)RaH, dadrUrogin.

RING (subs.): I A circle: q. v.: maRqalam, dancing in a r.: maRqalanftyam.II For fingers: aNgulI (rI) yam, -kam, interchange of r. s: aNgulIyaka- vinimayaH, D. ii.; r. -finger: anAmikA (but maDyamA, i. e. the middle finger is the Hindoo r. -f. Hence maDyamopalaH, Ki. ix. 2.); bezel of [Page601] a r.: maRibanDaH., -nam, Sa. v.III A circular area: maRqalam, vITiH (?).
RING (v. t.): I Of bells: cAlayati (c. of cal) (= to move). N.B. vAdayati (c. of vad) is of striking bells.II To fit with r. s: expr. by circumlo.III To encircle: parivezwayati (c. of vezw).
RING (v. i.): (1) kvaRati (kvaR, c. 1.);(2) raRati (raR, c. 1.): v. To sound.

RING , s. (Circle) maRqalaM, parimaRqalaM, cakraM, cakravAlaM, valayaH -yaM, varttulaH. — (Of metal) lohacakraM, lohavalayaH -yaM; ‘of a chain,’ lohalaH. — (Ornament for the finger) aNgulIyakaM, aNgurIyakaM, aNgurIyaH -yaM, aNgulIkaH -kaM, UrmmikA, karArowaH, bAlakaH; ‘seal-ring,’ aNguli- mudrA -drikA, mudrA, vadiH -dI f.; ‘ring for the toes or feet,’ nUpuraH, pAdANgadaM, pAdakawakaH, maYjIraM; ‘marriage-ring,’ kOtukaM, maNgalasUtraM, see MARRIAGE; ‘sacred ring of kuśa grass worn during religious ceremonies,’ pavitraM -trakaM. — (Circle of per- sons) maRqalaM; ‘dancing in a ring,’ maRqalanftyaM, hallIzaM -zakaM. — (Arena) raNgaH. — (Ringing sound) kvaRitaM, SiYjitaM, kvaRaH, zaRwA- SiYjitaM, GaRwASabdaH, JanatkAraH, JajJA -jJanaM.

To RING , v. a. (Cause to ring or sound, as a bell) GaRwAM vad (c. 10. vAdayati -yituM) or kvaR (c. 10. kvaRayati -yituM) or nad (c. 10. nAdayati -yituM), GaRwAm Ahan (c. 2. -hanti -ntuM), GaRwAkvaRanaM kf, GaRwAvAdanaM kf.

To RING , v. n. (Sound, as a bell) kvaR (c. 1. kvaRati -RituM), SiYj (c. 2. SiMkte, c. 1. SiYjate -YjituM), viSiYj, kiNkiRa (nom. kiNki- RAyate), Dvan (c. 1. Dvanati -nituM), prakzveq (c. 1. kzveqati -qituM), JajJA (nom. JajJAyate), kvaRitaM kf, SiYjitaM kf, JanatkAraM kf, GaRwAvat SabdaM kf.
RING-DOVE: kapotaviSezaH.
RING-LEADER: (1) nAyakaH: v. Leader;(2) muKayaH: v. Head, chief.
RING-LEADER , s. muKyaH, muKaraH, pramuKaH, pravarttakaH, prayojakaH, nAyakaH.
RING-WORM , s. koWaH, dadruH m., dadrUH m., gajakarRaM, KarjjUH f.
RINGED , a. (Fitted with rings) sANgulIyaH -yA -yaM, savalayaH -yA -yaM.
RINGER , s. GaRwAvAdakaH, GaRwAGAtI m. (n), GaRwAtAqakaH.
RINGING: I Subs.:(1) kvaRitam;(2) raRitam. II Adj.:(1) kvaRat (f. ntI);(2) raRat (f. ntI), raRadBiH svarEH, Si. i. 10.
RINGING , s. GaRwAvAdanaM, kvaRanaM, kvaRitaM, SiYjitaM, JajJanaM, JanatkAraH.
Ringlet, s. alakaH, cUrRakuMtalaH, kuralaH.
RINGLET: alakaH: v. Curl, hair. (1).
RINGLET , s. alakaH, alakAntaH, karkarAlaH, kuralaH. See CURL.
RINGWORM: dadru (drUH), -rogaH.
Rinse, v. t. jalena prakzal 10, (jalaM) upa-spfS 6 P, Acam 1 P. [Rins]ing, s. AcamanaM, upasparSaH.

RINSE (v.): I Of the mouth:(1) AcAmati (cam, c. 1.);(2) upaspfSati (spfS, c. 6.); drinking fountain water and r. ing (the mouth with it): pItvA prasravaRajalamupaspfSya ca, R.II To cleanse, wash: q. v.: prakzAlayati (kzal, c. 10.).

To RINSE , v. a. (Wash out the mouth) Acam (c. 1. -cAmati -camituM), AcamanaM kf, jalam or udakam upaspfS (c. 6. -spfSati -sprazwuM), upasparSaM kf, gaRqUzaM kf, SucipraRIM kf. — (Cleanse by the intro- duction of water) jalaM nikzipya SuD (c. 10. SoDayati -yituM) or prakzal or parizkf; ‘one who has rinsed his mouth,’ AcAntaH.
RINSING (subs.): (1) Acamanam, water for r.: AcamanIyam;(2) upasparSaH;(3) prakzAlaRam: for dif.: v. To rinse.
RINSING , s. (The mouth) AcamanaM, AcAmyaM, upasyarSaH, gaRqUzaH, SucipraRIH f.; ‘water for rinsing the mouth,’ AcamanIyaM, AcAmyaM.

Riot, s. saMmardaH, saMkzoBaH, tumulaM, kolAhalaH, viplavaH. 2 yaTecCapAnotsavaH, vizayasuKAti-rekaH, tumulotsavaH. 3 saM-ava-mardaH (saMBUya kftaH); rAjABidrohaH, prajAkzoBaH, prakftikopaH; ‘to run r(iot)’ maryAdAM atikram 1 U, 4 P or ati-i 2 P. v. i. saMkzoBaM i 2 P, saMraMBaM gam 1 P, tumulaM kf 8 U. 2 suKopaBoge nimagna a. BU 1 P, tumularaveRa utsavaM sev 1 A or kf. [Riot]er, s. tumulasaMkzoBakArin m. [Riot]ous, a. tumula-kzoBa-kArin, tumulotsava-kArin. [Riot]ously, adv. tumulaSabdena, sakolAhalaM.

RIOT (subs.): I Tumult, uproar: q. v.: saMkzoBaH.II In law: breach of the peace: perh.: samBUyABiGAtaH, -avamardaH or -aBidrohaH.III Revelry, excess q. v. Ph.: to run r.: expr. with niravagraha (f. hA), aniyantrita (f. tA), etc.; that (vicious elephant) has run r. in the highway: sa (duzwahastI) mahAntaM saMkzoBaM kurvan rAja- mArgamavatIrRaH, Mr. ii.
RIOT (v.): I To be greatly excited:(1) saMkzuByati (kzuB, c. 4.);(2) saramBaM gacCati (gam, c. 1.), etc.II To revel: q. v.

RIOT , s. (Tumult, uproar) tumulaM, kolAhalaH, qimbaH, qimbAhavaH, qamaraH, qAmaraH, viplavaH, AhavaH, kAlakIlaH, samBramaH camatkAraH. — (Popular disturbance) prakftikzoBaH, prajAkzoBaH, prakftiyudDaM, grAmayudDaM, grAmamadgu- rikA. — (Noisy festivity) atiSayaSabdena or atiSayatumulena utsava- karaRaM, see REVEL. — (To run riot) maryyAdAm atikram or laMG.
To RIOT , v. n. (Raise an uproar) tumulaM kf, kolAhalaM kf, qimbaM kf, viplavaM kf. — (Revel) atiSayaSabdena or atiSayatumulena utsavaM kf.
RIOTER: in law: samBUyABiGAtin (f. nI), avamardakArin (f. RI), etc.: v. Also reveller.
RIOTER , s. tumulakArI m. (n), qimbakArI m., kzoBakArI m., kzoBakft m.
RIOTOUS , a. tumulakArI -riRI -ri (n), kolAhalakArI &c., qimbakArI &c., mahASabdakArI &c., kzoBakArI &c., mahASabdena or atiSayatumulena utsavakArI &c.
RIOTOUSLY: (1) saMkzoBaM kurvat (f. ntI);(2) mahA- Sabdena (= noisily).
RIOTOUSLY , adv. atiSayatusulena, atitumulena, kolAhalena, mahASabdena.
Rip, v. t. vi-, dF 9 P or c., vipaw 10, nirBid 7 P, nikft 6 P; See Tear. s. vidaraH, vipAwanaM.
RIP (v.): pAwayati, vi- (paw, c. 10.): v. To tear, cut.
To RIP , v. a. (Tear) dF (c. 10. dArayati -yituM), vidF, paw (c. 10. pAwa- yati -yituM), vipaw, viBid, nikft, vinikft, vidAraRaM kf; ‘ripping open,’ vidAryya.
RIP , s. vidAraH -raRaM -RA, vidaraH, pAwanaM, vipAwanaM, viBedaH.
Riparian, a. nadItawasaMbaMDin.

Ripe, a. pakva, pari-vri-su-°, pakvatAM Apanna, pariRata, pAkonmuKa (KI f.), PalonmuKa, prOQa; ‘r(ipe) in years’ pari-Ratavayas, pravayas, pravfdDa, vayovfdDa; ‘r(ipe) to meet oneʼs doom’ vinASonmuKa, pakva. 2 sidDa, saMpanna; See Perfect. 3 sidDa, sajja, sannadDa; See Ready. Ripen, v. i. pAkaM i 2 P or vraj 1 P, pAkABimuKa-pAkonmuKa a. BU 1 P, pac pass., upaci pass.; ‘coldness r(ipen)ed into downright hatred’ anAdaraH (kAlakrameRa) upacIyamAnaH sAkzA-ddvezasya parAM kowiM iyAya. v. t. pac 1 P, kf with (a.), See Mature. [Ripen]ness, s. pari-vi-pAkaH, pariRati f., pariRAmaH, pakvA-vasTA, pakvadaSA.

RIPE: (1) pakva (f. kvA), pari-, vi-, saM-, with the rice r.: paripakvaSAliH, Ki. iv. 1.; thoroughly r. tumour: samyakpakvaH SoTaH, Bha.;(2) pariRata (f. tA), r. rose-apple: pariRatajambuPalam, Ki. x. 22.; r. poetic genius: pariRatakavitvaSaktiH, M.n.; (3) paktrima (f. mA), vi-, pari- (rare), by these r. words: vARIBirABiH paripaktrimABiH, N. xxii. 103.

RIPE , a. (As fruit, &c.) pakvaH -kvA -kvaM, paripakvaH &c., paktrimaH -mA -maM, vipaktrimaH &c., supakvaH -kvA -kvaM, pAkimaH -mA -maM, pakvatApannaH -nnA -nnaM, pakvadaSApannaH &c., pakvadaSAprAptaH -ptA -ptaM, pariRataH -tA -taM, pAkonmuKaH -KA -KaM, PalonmuKaH &c., vinASonmuKaH &c., SftaH -tA -taM. — (Brought to perfection, complete) sidDaH -dDA -dDaM, sampannaH -nnA -nnaM, vyutpannaH &c., prOQaH -QA -QaM. — (In years, &c.) pravfdDaH -dDA -dDaM, vfdDaH &c., prOQaH &c. — (Ready) udyataH -tA -taM, unmuKa in comp., see READY.

RIPEN: I Intrans.:(1) pAkam eti (i, c. 2.), gacCati, avApnoti, etc., r. ing: pAkaM vrajantI, Ri. iv. 11.;(2) pacati, pari-, (pac, c. 1.: rare), tumours r.: pacanti SoTAH, Bha. Ph.: about to r.: pAkonmuKa (f. KA), Bha.II Trans.: (1) pakvIkaroti;(2) pAkaM lamBayati (c. of laB), janayati (c. of jan), etc.;(3) pAcayati, vi-, pari- (c. of pac: rare), Bha.
To RIPEN , v. n. pakvaH -kvA -kvaM BU, paripakvaH -kvA -kvaM BU, pac in pass. (pacyate), paripac, pakvIBU, pakvatAM gam. See To MATURE, v. n.
To RIPEN , v. a. pac (c. 1. pacati, paktuM, c. 10. pAcayati -yituM), pakvaM -kvAM kf, paripakvaM -kvAM kf, pakvIkf, pAkaM kf or jan. See To MATURE, v. a.
RIPENED , p. p. pakvaH -kvA -kvaM, paripakvaH &c., pariRataH &c., see MATURED.

RIPENESS: (1) pAkaH, vi-, pari-, by the r. of the fruit: Palasya vipAkena, Ki. iv. 26.; resulting from the r. of purity: puRyaparipAkopAdAna (f. nA), Vi. iv.;(2) pakvatA, -tvam, pari-, vi-;(3) pariRAmaH; (4) pariRatiH.
RIPENESS , s. pAkaH, paripAkaH, pakvatA -tvaM, paripakvatA, paktiH f., vipAkraH, pakvaBAvaH, pakvadaSA, pakvAvasTA, pariRAmaH, pariRatiH f., pariRatatA. See MATURITY.
RIPENING , part. (Making ripe) pAcakaH -kA -kaM, pAcanaH -nA -naM, paripAkI -kiRI &c. — (Becoming ripe) pacyamAnaH -nA -naM, pari- pacyamAnaH &c.
Ripost, BaMgiBAzaRaM, sarasokti f.
RIPPED , p. p. vidAritaH -tA -taM, bidIrRaH -rRA -rRaM, vipAwitaH &c.
Ripple, s. taraMgaH, vIci-cI f., Urmi f., BaMgaH. v. i. kzuB 4 P, 1 A, calormi-sataraMga a. BU 1 P. [Rippl]ing, a. calormi, kzubDa, pracaladUrmi, sataraMga, taraMgAkula, uttaraMga.
RIPPLE: I Subs.:(1) budbudaH, U. ii. 46.;(2) taraNgaH (= wave: q. v.).II Verb: kzuByati (kzuB, c. 4.: to be agitated). R. ing (adj.): udbudbuda (f. dA).
RIPPLE , s. vIciH -cI f., vIcikA, UrmmiH -rmmI f., UrmmikA, sUkzmormmiH, BaNgiH f.
To RIPPLE , v. n. calormmiH -rmmiH -rmmi BU, calavIciH -ciH -ci BU, UrmmimAn -matI -mad BU, savIciH -ciH -ci BU, vIciBaNguraH -rA -raM BU.
To RIPPLE , v. a. vIciyuktaM -ktAM kf, vIcimantaM -matIM -mat kf, calavIciM kf.
RIPPLING , part. calormmiH -rmmiH -rmmi, calavIciH &c., vIcimAlI -linI &c.

Rise, v. i. utTA 1 P, samutTA 1 A, (in all senses); ‘r(isi)ing from the bed’ supto-tTita, muktaSayana; ‘do not r(ise) to receive their elders’ nAByuttizWaMti gurUn (Ka. 108). 2 udgam 1 P, ud-i 2 P, uday 1 A, utpat 1 P, UrDvaM gam or vraj 1 P, ud-vft 1 A; A-aDi-ruh 1 P, Akram 1 A (pUrva-diSaM); unnam 1 P. 3 pratiBA 2 P, nirBA, prAdurBU 1 P, AvirBU, dfS-lakz pass. 4 pra-, jan 4 A, utpad 4 A, pravft, ud-saM-pra-BU, niH-pra-sf, niH-gam. 5 (Advance) utTA, pra-, vfD 1 A, upaci- pass., aDikIBU, prabalatara a. BU; ‘r(isi)ing enemy’ uttizWamAnaH SatruH. 6 pra-tipattiM-unnatiM-prAp 5 P, unnam, utkfz pass. 7 (Against) aBidruh 4 P (with acc.), druh (with dat.), vyutTA 1 A. 8 (As sea) kzuB 1 A, 4 P, UrmimAlAkula-kzubDa a. BU. s. saM-, utTAnaM (fig. also). 2 udayaH, udgamaH-manaM, utpAtaH, UrDvagatiH; ‘he owes his r(ise) to me’ mattaH labDodayaH; ‘r(ise) and fall’ pAtotpAtO. 3 utpatti f., praBavaH, udBavaH, saMBavaH, udgamaH, pravftti f. pra-upa-kramaH, AraMBaH. 4 vfdDi f., upacayaH, ADikyaM. 5 unnati f., utkarzaH; pratipatti f. padavfdDiH, udayaH; ‘to give r(ise) to’ utpad c., jan c. [Ris]ing, s. utTAnaM, udayaH, udgamaH &c.; ‘r(ising) to receive another’ aByutTAnaM, pratyudgamaH. 2 prajA or pra-kfti-kzoBaH or prakopaH; See Mutiny. 3 Tumour, q. v.; ‘r(ising) ground’ unnataBUmiH, uccatTAnaM, utseDaH.

RISE (v.): I To appear:(1) udeti, udayati (i, c. 2. and 1.), r. ing slowly: mandamandamuditaH, Ki.; for the moon has r. n: udayati hi SaSANkaH, Mr. i. 54.;(2) udgacCati, as soon as the sun rose: yAvadevodagAtpataNgamaRqalam, D. ii.; clusters of clouds rose from (his) hair: udaguH...jalavAhAvalayaH SiroruheByaH, Si. xx. 66.;(3) uttizWate, sam-, (sTA, c. 1.), clouds are r. ing: meGaH samuttizWate, Mr. II To be up: uttizWati, rose from the bench: pIWAdudattizWat, Si. i. 12.; r. ing and washing our faces: utTAya ca DOtavaktrO, D. ii.; r. n breaking up the earth: BittvotTitaM BUmim, Si. iv. 1.; the bathing time having approached, the king dis- missed the chiefs and rose from the assembly- hall: samAsannasnAnasamayo visarjitarAjalokaH kziti- patirAsTAnamaRqapAduttasTO, K.III. To break out: uttizWate, a fire has r. n in the zenana: utTito'ntaH- [Page602] pure'gniH, Ra. iv. 14.; (if) he would r. to kill us: uttizWeta vaDAya naH, Vi. iv. 6.IV To advance: uttizWate, but a r. ing enemy: uttizWa- mAnastu paraH, Si. ii. 10.; some r. and fall, some fall and r.: ko'pyutTitaH patati, ko'pi patito'pyu- ttizWate, Mr. x.V To increase: q. v.: varDate (vfD, c. 1.) (as of rivers).

RISE (subs.): (1) utTAnam, sam-, newly r. n moon: navotTAna induH, R. vi. 31.; seeing him r.: tasyAByutTAnadarSinyaH, R. iv. 3.;(2) udayaH, -nam, aBi-, in (your) r.: udaye, R. viii. 84.; by their r. and setting: vyasanodayAByAm, Sa. iv. 2.; (3) udgamaH, -nam, sam-, (= appearance, as of heavenly bodies):(4) vfdDiH, vi- : v. Advancement, increase;(5) utpAtaH (oppo- -sed to fall: r. ing up, lit. and fig.), H. Ph. To give rise to: utpAdayati (c. of pad): v. To produce, beget.

To RISE , v. n. (Get up) utTA (c. 1. uttizWati -TAtuM, rt. sTA), samutTA; ‘he rose from his seat,’ AsanAd udasTAt or udatizWat; ‘from bed,’ SayanAd utTA, SayanaM or SayyAM tyaj, suptotTitaH -tA -taM BU. — (Move upward, ascend) UrdDvaM gam (c. 1. gacCati, gantuM), udgam, samu- dgam, uccEr gam, uccEr vraj (c. 1. vrajati -jituM), udi (c. 1. udayati c. 2. udeti -tuM, rt. i), samudi, aByudi, utpat (c. 1. -zatati -tituM), UrdDvam Akram (c. 1. -kramate -mituM), Akram, udvft (c. 1. -varttate -rttituM), Aruh (c. 1. -rohati -roQuM), uccar (c. 1. -carati -rituM), UrdDvagataH -tA -taM BU, udgataH -tA -taM BU, ArohaRaM kf; ‘the sun rises,’ udayati sUryyaH. The mountain behind which the heavenly bodies are supposed by the Hindus to rise is called udayaH, udayaparvataH &c., see MOUNTAIN. — (Become erect) unnam (c. 1. -namati -nantuM), unnataH -tA -taM BU, samunnam, utTA. — (Appear) dfS in pass. (-dfSyate), lakz in pass., utpad in pass., pratiBA (c. 2. -BAti -tuM), udBA, nirBA, praBU, AvirBU, prAdurBU, AtmAnaM dfS in caus. — (Originate, issue, take rise) utpad (c. 4. -padyate -pattuM), samutpad, jan (c. 4. jAyate, janituM), prajan, upajan, praBU, udBU, samBU, prasf (c. 1. -sarati -sarttuM), niHsf, viniHsf, udgam, nirgam, pravft (c. 1. -varttate -rttituM), udi, utpannaH -nnA -nnaM BU. — (Increase) vfD (c. 1. vaDeta -rDituM), pravfD, aDi- kIBU, aDikatarIBU, aDikataraH -rA -raM BU, uttarottaraM vfD. — (Be ex- cited) uddIptaH -ptA -ptaM BU, uddIp (c. 4. -dIppate -dIpituM), utpad in pass. — (From death) SmaSAnAd utTA or samutTA; all the dead. [Page694-a+ 51] rose, sarvve mftA udatizWanta. — (To heaven) svargArohaRaM kf. — (Be promoted) pratipattiM or padavfdDiM prAp, SrezWapade or utkfzwapade niyuktaH -ktA -ktaM BU. — (As the sea) kzubDaH -bDA -bDaM BU.

RISE , s. (Getting up) utTAnaM, samutTAnaM, utTitiH f. — (Moving upwards, ascent) UrdDvagamanaM, urdDvagatiH f., udgamaH -manaM, samudgamaH -manaM, udgatiH f., udayaH -yanaM, samudayaH, udvarttanaM, samutkramaH, utpAtaH, utpatanaM; ‘falls and rises,’ pAtotpAtAH m. pl.; ‘rise of the sun,’ sUryyodayaH. — (Origin, production) utpattiH f., udBavaH, udgamaH, samBavaH, praBavaH, pravfttiH f., mUlaM, AramBaH, AgamaH, upakramaH, upasTitiH f., upasTAnaM. — (Promotion) padavfdDiH f., pratipattiH f. — (Increase) vfdDiH f., pravfdDiH f., varDanaM. — (To give rise to) utpad (c. 10. -pAdayati -yituM), samutpad, jan (c. 10. janayati -yituM).

RISEN , p. p. utTitaH -tA -taM, aByutTitaH &c., samutTitaH &c., udgataH -tA -taM, samudgataH &c., pratyudgataH &c., uditaH &c., samuditaH &c., aByuditaH &c., utpatitaH -tA -taM, samutpatitaH &c., UrdDvagataH &c., udvarttitaH &c., udvfttaH -ttA -ttaM; ‘from bed or sleep,’ SayanotTitaH -tA -taM, supto- tTitaH &c., tyaktaSayyaH -yyA -yyaM, tyaktatalyaH -lyA -lyaM.
RISER: perh. utTAnakArin (f. RI); better by verb.
RISIBILITY: (1) hAsakaratvam, -tA and sim. comp. s.;(2) by adj.
RISIBILITY , s. hasanaSIlatA, hasanaSaktiH f., hasanecCA, hasanasAmarTyaM.
Risible, a. hAsajanana (nI f.), hAsyAspadaM, hAsakara (rI f.), hAsotpAdaka.
RISIBLE: (1) hAsakara (f. rI), Si. xv. 33.;(2) hAsajanana (f. nI); etc.
RISIBLE , a. hasanaSIlaH -lA -laM, hasanaSaktikaH -kA -kaM, hasanasamarTaH &c.,
RISING: I Adj.: expr. by pres. part.: v. To rise.II Subs.: v. Rise. Ph.: popular r.: prajAsaMkzoBaH: v. Tumult.

RISING , s. (Getting up) utTAnaM, samutTAnaM, utTitiH f., samutTitiH f., aByutTAnaM; ‘from a seat,’ AsanAdutTAnaM; ‘from bed,’ SayanAdu- tTAnaM; ‘rising to receive a visitor,’ pratyutTAnaM, pratyudgamaH -manaM, aByutTAnaM. — (Ascent, going upwards) udayaH -yanaM, udgamaH, udgatiH f., UrdDvagamanaM, UrdDvagatiH f., samudayaH, aByudayaH, samudgamaH, utpatanaM, samutpatanaM, utpAtaH, udvarttanaM, ArohaH -haRaM; ‘of the sun,’ sUryyodayaH; ‘of a planet,’ ucCrayaH; ‘of a sign,’ lagnaM, horA. — (Insurrection) prajAkzoBaH, prakftikzoBaH. — (Tumor), see the word.

RISING , part. udayI -yinI -yi (n), udayamAnaH -nA -naM, utpatan -tantI -tat (t), utpatitA -trI -tf (tf), utpatizRuH -zRuH -zRu, uditaH -tA -taM; ‘rising sun,’ praTamoditasUryyaH; ‘warmth of it,’ praTamoditAdityatApaH.
RISING-GROUND , s. unnataBUBAgaH, unnataBUmiBAgaH, uccaBUBAgaH, uccasTAnaM.
Risk, s. saMSayaH, saMdehaH, SaMkA, BayaM, saMkawaM, ‘run the r(isk) of losing all’ sarvanASa-saMSaye AtmAnaM pat c. v. t. saMSaye nikzip 6 P or pat c.; See Danger.
RISK: I Subs.: saNkawam: v. Danger, peril. II Verb.:(1) saMSaye, sandehe or saNkawe kzipati, ni-, (kzip, c. 6.), etc.:(2) saMSayasTaM (f. sTAM), etc. karoti.
RISK , s. saMSayaH, SaNkA, sandehaH, vikalyaH, BayaM, BayahetuH m., saNkawaM; ‘of life,’ jIvitasaMSayaH, see JEOPARDY, PERIL, DANGER.
To RISK , v. a. saMSayasTaM -sTAM kf, sandehasTaM -sTAM kf, SaNkAsTaM -sTAM kf, SaNkAspadIkf, SaNkAspadaM kf. See To JEOPARD, HAZARD.
RISKED , p. p. saMSayitaH -tA -taM, SaNkAspadIkftaH &c., sandehAspadIkftaH &c.

Rite, s. kriyA, viDiH, karman n., kAryaM, A-cAraH, saMskAraH, niyamaH, kalpaH; ‘scriptural r(ite)’ SAstraviDiH-karma, SAstroktakriyA. Ritual, a. vEDika-nEyamika- (kI f.), viDyanurUpa, SAstrokta, viDi-kriyA in comp. s. kriyA-saMrakAraH-viDiH-padDatiH-SAstraM. [Ritual]ist, s. saMskAraSAstrajYaH.
RITE (subs.): (1) kriyA;(2) viDiH;(3) karman (n.): v. Ceremony.

RITE , s. (Religious observance) kriyA, viDiH m., viDAnaM, karmma n. (n), devakarmma n., dEvakarmma n., devakriyA, dEvakriyA, devakAryyaM, dEvakAryyaM, saMskAraH, niyamaH, rItiH f., kalpaH, saMviDAnaM, AcAraH, AcaraRaM, SAstra- viDAnaM, SAstraviDiH m., SAstrakarmma n., SAstroktakarmma n., SAstraviDAnaM, SAstraviDiH m., anuzWAnaM, vrataM, yamaH, niyAmaH; ‘marriage rite,’ vivAhaviDiH m., see MARRIAGE; ‘funeral rite,’ uttarakriyA, antyakriyA, antasatkriyA, mftaSarIrasatkarmma n. (n), see OBSEQUIES, FUNERAL; ‘rite of investiture with the sacrificial thread,’ upanayanaM, see INVESTITURE; ‘rite of oblation to the manes,’ pitfkarmma n., pitfkriyA, see MANES. The following are the sanskaras, or rites purificatory of the bodies of the three classes in this life, and qualifying them for the next, ex- plained in Manu Bk 2. 27 et seq.: 1. Sacrifice on con- ception, garBADAnaM. 2. On the quickening of the fœtus, puMsavanaM. 3. A rite consisting of partition and arrangement of [Page694-b+ 51] the hair of the mother in the fourth, sixth, or eighth month of gestation, sImantonnayanaM. 4. Giving the new-born infant honey and clarified butter out of a golden spoon, before separating the navel-string, jAtakarmma n. 5. Naming the child on the tenth or twelfth day after birth, nAmakarmma n. or nAmakaraRaM. 6. Carrying the child out to see the sun in the fourth month after birth, nizkramaRaM. 7. Feeding the child with boiled rice in the sixth month after birth, or on the cutting of the first tooth, annaprASanaM. 8. Tonsure, or shaving the head all but one lock, in the first or third year after birth, cUqAkarmma n. or cUqAkaraRaM or cUqAkAryyaM. 9. Investiture with a peculiar thread or cord, called the sacrificial thread, worn over the left shoulder and under the right, per- formed on youths of the three classes at ages varying from eight to sixteen, from eleven to twenty-two, and from twelve to twenty-four, respectively, upanayanaM. 10. Cutting off the hair entirely, performed on Brahmans at sixteen on Kshatriyas at twenty-two, and on Vaiśyas at twenty- four years of age, keSAntaH. 11. Ceremony performed by youths of the first class on returning from the house of their preceptor to that of their natural parents, samAvarttanaM. 12. Marriage, in the thirty-sixth or eighteenth year, vi- vAhaH. — (Inauspicious rite) aSuBakarmma n. (n), aSuBakAryyaM; ‘rites and ceremonies,’ AcAravicArAH m. pl.; ‘performing a rite,’ kriyAnuzWAnaM; ‘mode of performing a rite,’ kriyAviDiH m., prayogaH.
RITUAL: I Adj.: by comp.: v. Ceremo- -rial.II Subs.: kriyApadDatiH (tI) and sim. comp. s.

RITUAL , a. (Pertaining to rites, consisting of them) vEDikaH -kI -kaM, vEDaH -DI -DaM, viDi in comp., viDirUpaH -pA -paM, viDimayaH -yI -yaM, viDyuktaH -ktA -ktaM, viDisambanDI -nDinI &c., viDivizayakaH -kA -kaM, kriyAsambanDI &c., kriyAvizayakaH &c., kriyA in comp., SAstroktaH -ktA -ktaM, AcArikaH -kI -kaM, kAlpaH -lpI -lpaM.
RITUAL , s. kriyApadDatiH -tI, saMskArapadDatiH f., karmmapadDatiH f., viDipadDatiH f., viDAnapadDatiH f., padDatiH -tI, saMskAraSAstraM, viDiSAstraM, kriyAviDiH m., viDiH m.
RITUALIST: kriyApadDatijYa (f. jYA) and sim. comp. s.
RITUALIST , s. kriyAviDijYaH, saMskAraSAstrajYaH, kriyAvAn m. (t).

Rival, v. t. sparD 1 A, prati-pari-°, (with instr.), saMGfz 1 P, ahamahamikayA-paraspara-jigIzayA-yat 1 A, vi-, ji desid. (ji-gIzati); oft. by pratidvaMdvin, pratisparDin; ‘with hands r(ivall)ing young foliage (in beauty)’ kisalayodBedapratidvaMdviBiH karatalEH (S. 4); caMdracCAyApratisparDI or -pratidvaMdvI &c. a., s. prati-, sparDin, pratiyogin, vi-, jigIzu, pratipakza, sapatna, parasparasaMGarzin, aBiBavecCu; by prati in comp. ‘r(ival) combatant’ pratiyoDaH; ‘r(ival) army’ pratibalaM &c.; ‘r(ival) woman’ sapatnI; ‘a r(ival) Kesava’ aparaH keSavaH, pratikeSavaH; ‘a r(ival) to Sri’ pratyAdeSa iva SriyAH (V. 1). [Rival]ry, s. pratisparDA, pratiyogitA, vi-, jigIzA, ahamahamikA, pratidvaMdvitA, saMGarzaH, sApatnyaM, pratipakzatA; viroDaH, vEraM.

RIVAL (subs. and adj.): (1) often by prati- in comp., r. combatant: pratidvandvin (f. nI), R. vii. 37.; r. lady: pratiyuvatiH, Si. viii. 38.; r. elephant: pratidvipaH, Ki. xvii. 45.;(2) samAna (f. nA = equal), r. s in learning are as a rule jealous of each other's fame: prAyaH samAnavidyA parasparayaSaHpuroBAgAH, Mal. i. 19.;(3) pratiyogin (f. nI);(4) sapatnI (a r. wife), r. rills: sapatnI- rnimnagAH, Si. ii. 104.
RIVAL (v.): I To emulate: q. v.: sparDate (sparD, c. 1.).II To excel: q. v.: atiSete (SI, c. 2.).
RIVAL , s. sparDI m. (n), pratisparDI m., pratiyogI m. (n), pratipakzaH, sapatnaH, vijigIzuH m., jigIzuH m., see RIVAL, a.; ‘a kingdom without a rival,’ asapatnaM rAjyaM; ‘a rival wife,’ sapatnI.

RIVAL , a. sparDI -rDinI -rDi (n), visparDI &c., pratisparDI &c., pari- sparDI &c., pratiyogI &c., vijigIzuH -zuH -zu, jigIzuH &c., paraspa- ravijigIzuH &c., parasparABiBavecCuH -cCuH -cCu, ekArTecCuH &c., ekA- rTABilAzI &c., ekArTI &c., ekArTadfzwiH -zwiH -zwi, ekArTapravfttaH -ttA -ttaM, ekArTodyuktaH -ktA -ktaM, saMGarpI &c., parasparasaMGarzI &c., jayecCuH &c. aBiBavecCuH &c.

To RIVAL , v. a. sparD (c. 1. sparDate -rDituM), visparD, pratisparD, AsparD with instr. c., ji in des. (jigIzati -zituM), viji in des., parABiBavanAya or parasparABiBavanAya yat (c. 1. yatate -tituM) or udyogaM kf, parajayArTaM yat, parasparaM saMGfz (c. 1. -Garzati -rzituM), ekArTam aBi- lap or AkAMkz, ekArTaprApaRAya yat; ‘he rivals Indra,’ SakreRa or SakreRa saha sparDate; ‘one who rivals the beauty of the moon,’ candracCAyAparisparDI.
RIVALING , RIVALLING, part. sparDI -rDinI &c. See RIVAL, a.
RIVALRY: (1) sparDA (= emulation);(2) prati- yogitA (= competition);(3) viroDaH (= con- -test, opposition: q. v.).

RIVALRY , s. sparDA or spardDA, pratisparDA, AsparDA, jigIzA, vijigIzA, pratiyogitA -tvaM, pratipakzatA -tvaM, sApatnyaM, sapatnatvaM, saMGarzaH, parasparasaMGarzaH, parABiBavecCA, parasparABiBavecCA, parasparABiBavanAya udyogaH, parajayecCA, parasparajayecCA, ekArTABilAzaH, ekArTAkAMkzA, ekArTaprApaRAya parasparo- dyogaH, ekArTadfzwiH f., ekArTapravfttiH f., ahampUrvvikA.
RIVE: vidArayati (c. of dF): v. To tear, split.
RIVEN , p. p. vidIrRaH -rRA -rRaM, vidAritaH -tA -taM, CinnaH -nnA -nnaM, viBinnaH &c.

River, s. nadI, sarit, siMDuH, A(a)pagA, nimnagA, taraMgiRI, srotovahA, tawinI, hrAdinI, srotasvinI, DunI, SEvalinI, dvIpavatI, sravaMtI, nirJariRI ‘a small r(iver)’ kulyA, alpa-kftrima-sarit; ‘confluence of r(iver)s’ saMBedaH, siMDusaMgamaH; ‘watered by r(iver)s’ nadImAtfka.

RIVER: (1) nadI (or nadaH, of a few r. s — the Indus sinDuH, the Brahmaputra brahmaputraH or lOhityaH, the Śon SoRaH, etc.), r. bank: nadIkUlam; r. diver: nadIzRaH, R. xvi. 75.; r. -irrigated: nadImAtfka (f. kA), M.n. on Ki. i. 17.; r. fish: nAdeyo matsyaH;(2) sarit (f.);(3) sinDuH (f.: rare); (4) ApagA, Sr.; nimnagA, taraqgiRI, srotasvatI, etc. (poet.);(5) DunI (or niH: rare), A.

RIVER , s. nadI, sarit f., sinDuH f., apagA, nimnagA, srotas n., kulyA, srotovahA, SrotovahA, srotasvatI, srotasvinI, payasvinI, sravantI, dravantI, samudragA, jalaDigA, sAgaragAminI, taraNgiRI, tawinI, SEvalinI, hradinI, hrAdinI, parvvatajA, roDovakrA, roDavakrA, samudradayitA, samudrakAntA, kUlavatI, kUlaNkazA, DunI, DenA, jambAlinI, dvIpavatI, nirGUriRI, udyaH, nadaH. This last is applied only to a river of which the personification is male, as the Indus sinDuH, Brahma- putra brahmaputraH, Śona SoRaH, hiraRyabAhuH; ‘bed of a river,’ nadIpAtraM, nadIBARqaM; ‘bank of a river,’ nadItIraM, nadIkUlaM; ‘cur- rent,’ nadIvegaH, nadIrayaH, nadIvelA; ‘water of a river,’ sarijjalaM; ‘source,’ sarinmuKaM; ‘mouth,’ sinDusaNgamaH, samBedaH; ‘watered by rivers,’ nadImAtfkaH -kA -kaM, jalamAtfkaH &c.; ‘one who knows the course of rivers,’ nadIjYaH; ‘bathing in a river,’ nadIzRaH -zRA -zRaM; ‘the bend of a river,’ nadIvaNkaH; ‘relating to a river,’ nAdeyaH -yI -yaM. — (River of heaven), svarRadI, sura- nadI, see GANGES, MILKY-WAY.

Rivet, v. t. kIl 10, kIlena baMD 9 P, dfQaM baMD; aBiniviS c., sasj c.; ‘to be r(ivett)ed’ kIlita-dfQabadDa a. RIVET , s. kIlaH -lakaH, lohakIlakaH, sUkzmakIlakaH, SalAkA.

Road, s. mArgaH, paTin m., aDvan m., vartman n., vITi-TI f., raTyA, saraRi-RI f., padavI, padDati-tI f.; ‘high r(oad)’ rAjamArgaH-paTaH; ‘common r(oad)’ pracAraH; ‘difficult r(oad)’ durga-saMcaraH, saMkramaH, durgamArgaH; ‘dreary, lonely r(oad)’ prAMtaraM, SUnyamArgaH; ‘crossing of r(oad)s’ catuzpaTaM, SfgAwakaM; See Way.

ROAD: (1) mArgaH, high r.: rAjamArgaH; of r. -side trees: mArgaSAKinAm, R. i. 45.; looking for r. s: mArgEzin (f. RI), R. xvi. 31.;(2) paTin (m.: paTa- in comp. s), although the r. is not straight to you: vakraH panTA yadapi BavataH, Me. i. 28.; making and clearing r. s in the dense forest: kurvantaH SoDayantaSca panTAno gahane vane, Ram. ii. 87. 7.; bad r. (i. e. vicious course): apanTAH, An. i. 4.; where four r. s meet: catuzpaTam, Mit.;(3) aDvan (m.), on the r.: aDvani, R. v. 60.; the remainder of the r.: aDvaSezam, Me. i. 39.; (4) vartman (n.), from the beaten r.:, kzuRRAdvartmanaH, R. i. 17.;(5) raTyA (= high r.), r. embellish- ment: raTyAsaMskAraH, R. xv. 38.

(n), padvaH, upanizkramaRaM, saYcaraH, ekapadI, ekapAd, taraH, vITiH f., SaraRiH f., mAcaH, mAWaH, mAWyaH, prapATaH, pitsalaM, KullamaH; ‘public road, high road,’ rAja- mArgaH, rAjapaTaH, mahApaTaH, mahAvartma n.; ‘a good road,’ supaTaH, supanTAH m., atipanTAH m., satpaTaH, sanmArgaH; ‘a bad road,’ kupaTaH, kumArgaH, kApaTaH, vipaTaH, kadaDvA m. ROAM (v.): (1) Bramati or BrAmyati, pari-, (Bram, c. 1. and 4.), r. ing over countries: BrAntvA deSam, J.;(2) awati, pari-, (aw, c. 1.), one day r. ing: ekadA paryawan, D.

ROAN , a. (Horse) Suklavinducitrito nIlavarRASvaH or SyAmavarRASvaH.

Roar, v. i. garj 1 P, stan 1 P, nard 1 P, ras 1 P, ru 2 P, nad 1 P, anu-huMkf 8 U (of lion); ‘a r(oar)ing river’ GarGararavA sarin. 2 vi-A-ut-vyAkruS 1 P, praRad, Guz 10; ‘r(oar)ing with pain’ ArtanAdaM muM-can. [Roar]ing, s. garjita, stanita, garjanaM-nA, nardanaM, virAvaH, mahA-dIrGa-gaMBIra-SabdaH-nAdaH; GanaDvaniH, dIGarAvaH-GozaH; huMkAraH. 2 nAdaH, vi-A-kroSaH, niGozaH, SabdaH, svaraH, DvaniH.

Noise.II In distress: kroSati, vi-, (kruS, c. 1.): v. To cry.
ROAR, -ING (subs.): (1) garjanam or garjitam, pari-; (2) stanitam;(3) huMkAraH, -kftiH(taM): v. Also cry, noise, scream.

To ROAR , v. n. (Make a loud continued sound) garj (c. 1. garjati -rjituM), parigarj, nard (c. 1. nardati -rdituM), vinard, ru (c. 2. rOti, ravituM), viru, saMru, ras, vAS, raw, gaj, hamB (nom. hamBAyate -yituM), huNkf, hUNkf, huNkAraM kf, anuhuNkf, garjanaM kf. — (Cry out, bawl) nad (c. 1. nadati -dituM), vinad, praRad, utkruS (c. 1. -kroSati -krozwuM), vikruS prakruS, citkAraM kf, cItkAraM kf, cIt SabdaM kf, Guz, prakzviq (c. 1. kzveqati -qituM), nAdaM kf; ‘from pain,’ ArttanAdaM kf.

ROAR , ROARING, s. (Loud continued sound) garjanaM -nA, garjitaM, parigarjanaM, nardanaM, narditaM, rAvaH, virAvaH, dIrGaDvaniH m., dIrGarAvaH, dIrGarutaM, dIrGanirGozaH, rAsaH, hamBA, hamBArAvaH, GanaDvaniH m., gamBI- raSabdaH, gamBIraDvaniH m., huNkAraH, huNkutaM, huNkftiH f., sUtkAraH, cukkAraH, GarDaritaM. — (Crying out) nAdaH, utkroSaH, citkAraH, cItkAraH, GozaH, nirGozaH, udGozaH, utkruzwaM, vikruzwaM, kzveqitaM, prakzveqitaM. — (Of a lion) siMhanAdaH -dakaH, siMhaDvaniH m., siMhanardaH -rdanaM. — (Of the clouds) meGanirGozaH, GanaDvaniH m., meGanAdaH, meGagarjanaM, GanaSabdaH, GanasvanaH. — (Of the sea) samudranAdaH, mahArRavasvanaH.

ROOK , s. kAkajAtIyaH pakzI, kAkaH, vAyasaH. See CROW.
ROOKERY: kAkASrayaH or in gen. KagASrayaH and sim. comp. s.
ROOKERY , s. kAkASrayaH, kAkAlayaH, kAkASayaH, kAkasTAnaM, kAkAyatanaM.

Room, s. veSman n., pra-, kozWaH, SAlA, kakzaH-kzA, kuwI, gfhaM; ‘upper r(oom)’ caMdraSAlA, Si-rogfhaM; ‘inner r(oom)’ garBAgAraM, vAsagfhaM, aMtaH-kozWaH. 2 pra-, deSaH, sTAnaM, AspadaM, BUmi f., padaM; sa vAsavena ito nizIdeti visfzwaBUmiH (K. iii. 2) ‘Vasava made r(oom) for him’ &c.; ‘there is r(oom) for doubt here’ SaM-kAsTAnametat. 3 avakASaH, avasaraH, prasaraH, vizayaH, aMtaraM, sTalaM; ‘want of r(oom)’ anava-kASaH, sTalasaMkocaH; ‘giving no r(oom) for envy’ adattAvakASo matsarasya; ‘make r(oom)’ aMtaraM dIyatAM, apasara. 4 (Stead) sTAnaM, BUmiH; See Instead of. [Room]y, a. viSAla, vistIrRa, vipula, asaMbADa, sAvakASa.
ROOM: I Space: q. v.: avasaraH.II Place: q. v.: BUmiH.III An apartment: kozWaH. Top-r.:(1) candraSAlA;(2) Sirogfham.

ROOM , s. (Space, compass, free course) avakASaH, prasaraH, avasaraH, antaraM, vizayaH, apasAraRaM; ‘want of room,’ anavakASaH; ‘the water flows out to make room for the stone,’ pAzARAya vizayaM dattvA jalaM vahirgacCati; ‘room! make room!’ apasara, avasara. — (Place for reception or admission of any thing) sTAnaM, AspadaM, padaM, BUmiH f., pradeSaH; ‘room for suspicion,’ SaNkAspadaM; ‘room for fear,’ BayasTAnaM; ‘there was no room to hold all,’ sarvvaDAraRAya sTAnaM nABavat. — (Opportunity) avasaraH, avakASaH. — (Stead, lieu) sTAnaM, sTalaM, BUmiH f.; ‘in the room of,’ sTAne, BUmO, sTale. — (Apartment) SAlA -likA, AgAraH -raM, kozWaH -zWakaM, gfhaM, kakzaH, kuwI, AvAsaH, prakozWaH, sTalaM -lI; ‘inner room,’ upa- roDakaM, antargfhaM, garBagfhaM, garBAgAraM, garBaH; ‘top room, upper room,’ SirogfhaM, candraSAlikA, upariSAlA.
ROOMINESS: (1) asambADatA;(2) viSAlatA;(3) vistIrRatA.
ROOMINESS , s. sAvakASatvaM, vistIrRatA, viSAlatA, asambADatA, vipulatA.
ROOMY: (1) asambADa (f. DA);(3) viSAla (f. lA): v. Spacious, large.
ROOMY , a. sAvakASaH -SA -SaM, asambADaH -DA -DaM, vistIrRaH -rRA -rRaM, vipulaH -lA -laM, viSAlaH -lA -laM, vistftaH -tA -taM.
Roost, s. vAsayazwi f., yazwinivAsaH, nilayana or Sayana-daMqaH or sTAnaM. v. i. SI 2 A, svap 2 P, nilI 4 A, nizad 1 P, ASri 1 U.
ROOST: I Subs.:(1) vAsayazwiH;(2) yazwinivAsaH, R. xvi. 14.; and sim. comp. s.II Verb: Sete (SI, c. 2.), r. ing on trees: vfkzeSayAH, R.
ROOST , s. pakziRAM vAsayazwiH m. or nivAsayazwiH m. or SayanayazwiH, pakziRAM vAsadaRqaH or vAsasTAnaM or nilayanasTAnaM.

To ROOST , v. n. pakzivat taruSAKAyAM or daRqAgre svap (c. 2. svapiti -tuM) or SI (c. 2. Sete, SayituM), yazwyagre or taruSAKAyAM svaptArTaM nilI (c. 4. -lIyate -letuM) or nivas or aDivas or vas or nizad or avasTA or ASri.
ROOSTING , part. taruSAKAyAM nilIyamAnaH -nA -naM, taruSAyI -yinI -yi (n).

Root, s. mUlaM, in all senses; tarumUlaM, kalahamUlaM &c.; aMGriH, pAdaH (Foot, q. v.); bu(bra)DnaH; SiPA, jawA (fibrous); ‘bulbous r(oot)’ kaMdaH-daM; ‘to the r(oot)s’ AmUlaM, mUlataH, samUlaM; ‘the r(oot) of a branch’ avarohaH. 2 aDoBAgaH-deSaH, talaM, mUlaM, jAhaM in comp. (of animals only). 3 mUlaM, bIjaM, yoni f., AdiH, nidAnaM, kAraRaM, AdibIjaM-kA-raRaM-hetuH, prakfti f.; ‘having for its r(oot)’ mUla, hetu, &c. in comp.; vittamUlaH kalahaH, &c. 4 (Of a word) mUlaM, prakftiH; Sabda-yoniH; ‘r(oot)-meaning’ mUlArTaH, yOgikArTaH, vyutpattisidDaH. 5 (Of numbers) mUlaM, padaM; ‘to extract a r(oot)’ mUlIkf 8 U. v. t. ‘take r(oot)’ mUlaM baMD 9 P. v. t. dfQaM niKan 1 P or ruh c.; ex. by ‘r(oot)ed’. 2 (Up) unmUl 10, samUlaM ud-hf 1 P, utpaw 10, utKan, vyaparuh c., ucCid 7 P. [Root]ed, a. dfQa-badDa-mUla, rUQa-Dfta-mUla.

ROOT (subs.): I Lit.: BUlam, r. of a tree: tarumUlam, Sa.; a hurricane does not pluck up grass by the r.: tfRAni nonmUlayati praBaYjanaH, H. ii. 81. Ph.: Fibrous r.: SiPA or jawA; bulbous r.: kanda (mn.).II Fig.: mUlam, the r. of faults: mUlaM dozasya, Ki. xi. 20.; with pure progeny from the r.: AmUlaSudDasantati, Sa. vi. 28.; destroying by the r.: samUlaGAtamaGnantaH, Si. ii. 33.; firmly taken r.: sTirabadDamUla (f. lA), B. xi. 5.: v. Also cause, source.III In arith.: mUlam, cube r.: GanamUlam, Li.; to extract a r.: mUlI- karoti, A.c.IV Of words: prakftiH. Ph.: verbal r.: DAtuH; secondary r.: nAmaDAtuH; names are derived from r. s: nAma ca DAtujam, Kāśikā.
ROOT (v.): mUlaM baDnAti (banD, c. 9.). R. ed: (1) badDamUla (f. lA);(2) rUQamUla (f. lA), M.n. on Si. i. 38. R. up or out: unmUlayati.

ROOT s. (That part of a plant or tree which enters the earth) mUlaM, aMGriH m., aMhriH m., braDnaH, vraGnaH, pAdaH, caraRaH -RaM, padaM, vfkzamUlaM, vfkzAMGriH m.; ‘firm roots,’ dfQamUlaM, DaraRamUlaM; ‘having firm roots,’ dfQamUlaH -lA -laM, badDamUlaH &c.; ‘to the roots, by the roots,’ AmUlaM, samUlaM, mUlatas; ‘to pluck up by the roots,’ unmUl (c. 10. -mUlayati -yituM), samUlaM or AmUlam utpaw; ‘from root to top,’ AmUlaSiKaraM, AmUlacUqaM; ‘to take root,’ mUlaM banD; ‘fibrous root,’ SiPA, jawA; ‘from a radicant branch,’ ava- rohaH; ‘bulbous root,’ kandaH -ndaM; ‘root-digger,’ mUlotpAwajIvI m. — (Lower part of any thing) aDoBAgaH, aDamaBAgaH, jAhaH; the latter is only applied to parts of the body of animals; as, ‘the root of the tail,’ pucCajAhaH; ‘of the hair,’ keSajAhaH. — (Original, source, first cause) mUlaM, vIjaM, yoniH m. f., AdiH m., hetuH m., mUlahetuH m., praTamahetuH m., nidAnaM, kAraRaM, mUla- kAraRaM, AdikAraRaM, AdihetuH m., garBaH; ‘having for its root,’ mUla or mUlaka in comp.; as, ‘happiness, having its root in contentment,’ santozamUlakaM suKaM; ‘strife having its root in avarice,’ loBamUlaH kalahaH. — (Root of a word, radical word) [Page697-b+ 51] SabdayoniH f., prakftiH f.; ‘relation of a root to its ramifica- tion,’ prakftivikftiBAvaH. — (Of a number) mUlaM. — (Of a square or cube) padaM, mUlaM; ‘square root,’ vargamUlaM, vargapadaM; ‘cube- root,’ GanamUlaM, GanapadaM.

To ROOT , v. a. (Plant deep in the earth) badDamUlaM -lAM kf, dfQamUlaM -lAM kf, dfQaM ruh in caus. (ropayati -yituM), dfQaM niKan, dfQaropaRaM kf. — (Root up) unmUl (c. 10. -mUlayati -yituM), samunmUl, mUlAt or samUlam udDf (c. 1. -harati -harttuM) or samudDf or utpaw (c. 10. -pAwayati yituM) or ucCid (c. 7. -Cinatti -CettuM) or vyaparuh in caus.
To ROOT , v. n. mUlaM banD (c. 9. baGnAti, bandDuM), badDamUlaH -lA -laM BU.
ROOTED , p. p. badDamUlaH -lA -laM, dfQamUlaH &c.; ‘rooted up,’ unmU- litaH -tA -taM, ucCinnamUlaH -lA -laM, nikfttamUlaH &c., udDftamUlaH &c., utpAwitaH -tA -taM, utKAtaH &c.
ROOTLET: SiPA or jawA (= fibrous root).

Rope, s. rajju f., guRaH, dAman f. n., SulvaM, varAwakaH-kaM, saMdAnaM, vawaH-wI-waM; ‘the rope and bucket of a well’ udGAwanaM, GawI-yaMtraM; ‘r(ope)-dancer’ sUtrAyaRaH, kalAyaRaH; ‘r(ope)-ladder’ rajjusopAnaM; ‘r(ope)-maker’ rajjukAraH. [Rop]y, a. rajjuDarman, SyAna, sAMdra.
ROPE: (1) rajjuH;(2) dAman (nf.): v. Also band.

ROPE , s. rajjuH m. f., guRaH, sUtraM, dAmA f. (n), dAma n. (n), dAmanI, varAwakaH, varAwaH, vawAkaraH, SulvaH, pASaH, sandAnaM, SullaM, galaH, pavitrakaM, vawaH -wI -waM, udvAhinI, suzmaM, pARisaryyA, vawIguRaH; ‘of a ship,’ nOrajjuH m. f.; ‘of a well,’ udGAwanaM, GawIyantraM; ‘hanging by a rope,’ rajcavalambI m. (n).
To ROPE , v. n. rajjuM vanD, sUtraM banD, sUtrarUpeRa vitatIBU.
ROPE-DANCER: (1) kalAyanaH;(2) sUtrAyaRaH.
ROPE-DANCER , s. kalAyanaH, sUtrAyanaH, rajjuyAyI m. (n), plavakaH, kelakaH.
ROPE-LADDER , s. rajjunirmmitasopAnaM, sUtrasopAnaM, rajjusopAnaM.
ROPE-MAKER , s. rajjukAraH -rakaH, rajjukArI m. (n), rajjukft, guRakAraH.
ROPE-WALK: perh. rajjuSAlA, rajjunirmARaSAlA, etc.
ROPINESS: cikkaRatA,: v. Stinginess, adhesive- -ness.
ROPINESS , s. rajjutvaM, guRatvaM, sasUtratA, sUtrapUrRatA, sAndratA, SyAnatA.
ROPY: fig.: cikkaRa (f. RA): v. Glutinous, viscous.
ROPY , a. rajjuguRakaH -kA -kaM, SyAnaH -nA -naM, sUtramayaH -yI -yaM.
Rosary, s. akzamAlA, akzasUtraM, japamAlA-sUtraM.
ROSARY: I Lit.: perh. sevatogrAmaH.II Devo- -tional:(1) akzamAlA;(2) akzasUtram;(3) japamAlA.
ROSARY , s. japamAlA, akzamAlA, akzasUtraM, japasUtraM, mAlA, sUtraM, smaraRI; ‘fingers used as a rosary,’ karamAlA.

Rose, s. japApuzpaM, oqrapuzpaM; (tree or flower) japA-vA; sevatI, SatapatrI; ‘r(ose)-apple’ jaMbu-bU f.; (fruit) jaMbuPalaM, jAMbavaM. [Ros]y, a. pAwala, japAvarRa. 2 javArUpa. Roseate, a. ‘r(oseate)-coloured’ pAwala, japAsavarRa. 2 bahiH ramaRIya, dfzwimanohara.
ROSE: (1) sevatI;(2) SatapatrI;(3) lAkzA, Bha.; oil of r.: lAkzAtElam (?); r. -water: sevatItElam (?). China-r.: javA(pA). R. -apple (both the tree and its fruit) jambUH. R. -wood: dAruviSezaH.
ROSE , s. (The tree) javApuzyaH, oqrapuzyaH, piRqapuzpaH, hemapuzpaH, javA, japA, oqraH, uqraH, uQraH. — (Flower) javA, japA, javApuzpaM, oqrapuzpaM, hemapuzpaM.
ROSE-APPLE , s. (The tree) jambUH f., jambuH f., jambukaH, jambUkaH; ‘a large kind,’ rAjajambUH f. — (The fruit) jambUH f., jambuH f., jambu n., jAmbavaM, jambuPalaM.
ROSE-COLORED , ROSEATE, a. pAwalaH -lA -laM, pAwalavarRaH -rRA -rRaM, javAvarRaH &c.
ROSE-WATER , s. puzpadravaH, javApuzpadravaH, javApuzpajalaM.
ROSEMARY: latAviSezaH.
ROSTRUM: I Platform: pIWaH.II Beak: caYcuH.
ROSY: (1) pAwala (f. lA);(2) rAjat (f. ntI = blooming).
ROSY , a. (Rose-colored) pAwalaH -lA -laM, javAvarRaH -rRA -rRaM. — (Formed like a rose, full of roses) javArUpaH -pA -paM, javAmayaH -yI -yaM.

Rot, v. i. pUtIBU 1 P, vi-, gal 1 P, vilI 4 A, durgaMDa a. BU. v. t. gal c., vilI c., pUtIkf 8 U. Rotten, a. pUtigaMDi, durgaMDa, vigalita, vilIna; pUtIBUta, duzwa, dUzita. 2 kzIRasattva, asAra, niHsattva.
ROT (v.): I Intrans:(1) pUtIBavati (= put- -refy);(2) galati (gal, c. 1. = be decom- -posed).II Trans.:(1) pUtIkaroti;(2) gAlayati (c. of gal). For fig. sense: v. To spoil, corrupt.
To ROT , v. n. gal (c. 1. galati -lituM), vigal, galitaH -tA -taM BU, vi- galitaH -tA -taM, BU, vilI (c. 4. -lIyate -letuM), pravilI, kzi (c. 4. kzIyate), durganDaH -nDA -nDaM BU.
To ROT , v. a. gal (c. 10. galayati, gAlayati -yituM), vigal, galitIkf, vigalitIkf, vilI in caus. (-lApayati -yituM).

Rotate, v. t. Bram 1, 4 P, cakragatyA Bram, parivft 1 A; See Revolve. [Rotat]ion, s. BramaRaM, BrAMti f., A-pari-vartaH-vftti f., cakrA-vartaH, cakragatiH. 2 paryAyaH, kramaH, AnupUrvyaM; ‘in r(otation)’ paryAyeRa, paryAyavfttyA, cakravat, paryAyAnusAreRa, anupUrvaM. [Rotat]ory, Rotary, a. cakrAvartin, cakragati.
ROTATION: I Revolution: q. v.: cakraBramaRam, from the r. of the planets round the earth: grahARAM BUmeH parito BramaRataH, A.c.II Succession: paryAyavfttiH, in r.: paryAyeRa.

ROTATION , s. (Circular motion of a wheel, &c.) AvarttaH -rttanaM, AvfttiH f., parivarttaH -rttanaM, parivfttiH f., cakrAvarttanaM, cakrAvarttaH, cakra- gatiH f., BramaRaM, BrAntiH f., GUrRanaM, GUrRiH f. — (Vicissitude of suc- cession) paryyAyaH, paryyayaH, viparyyayaH, AnupUrvyaM, AnupUrvI, kramaH, pari- varttanaM; ‘in rotation,’ paryyAyeRa, paryyAyAnusAreRa, paryyAyAnukrameRa, cakravat.
ROTATORY, ROTARY: r. motion cakraBramaRam.

ROTATORY , ROTARY, a. cakravadAvarttI -rttinI -rtti (n), cakrAvarttI &c., cakravatparivarttI &c., cAkrikaH -kI -kaM, cakragatiH -tiH -ti, cakragAmI -minI &c.; ‘rotatory motion,’ cakrAvarttaH, cakravadAvarttaH.
Rote, s. Avftti f., aByAsaH, AvartanaM; ‘learn by r(ote)’ (arTajYAnaM vinA) kaMwasTa a. kf 8 U, aByas 4 U; ‘learnt by r(ote)’ kaMWasTa, aByasta.
ROTE: (1) AvfttiH;(2) aByAsaH. Ph.: learnt by r.:(1) muKasTa (f. sTA):(2) kaRWasTa (f. sTA).

ROTE , s. SabdAvarttanaM, SabdAvfttiH f., SabdamAtrAvarttanaM, AvarttanaM, aByAsaH, aByasanaM, rUpaM; ‘to learn by rote,’ SabdAvarttanaM kf, aByas (c. 4. [Page698-a+ 51] -asyati -situM); ‘learnt by rote,’ muKasTaH -sTA -sTaM, kaRWasTaH &c., aByastaH -stA -staM.
ROTTEN: I Putrid: pUta (f. tA).II Defec- -tive, spoiled: duzwa (f. zwA).

ROTTEN , a. galitaH -tA -taM, vigalitaH &c., vilInaH -nA -naM, viSIrRaH -rRA -rRaM, SIrRaH &c., kzIRaH -RA -RaM, pUtaH -tA -taM, pUtIBUtaH &c., durganDaH -nDA -nDaM. — (Unsound) kzIRasAraH -rA -raM, kzIRasattvaH -ttvA -ttvaM, asAraH -rA -raM.
ROTTENNESS: I Putridity: pUtiH.II Un- -soundness: duzwatA.
ROTTENNESS , s. galitatvaM -tA vigalitatvaM, kzIRatA, vilInatA, pUtatvaM, asAratA.
ROTUNDA (o): perh. sarvatoBadram, Mat. 253. ch.
ROTUNDA , ROTUNDO, s. varttulagfhaM, varttulaBavanaM, varttulaSAlA.
ROTUNDITY: vartulatA: v. Roundness.
ROUGE (v.): maYjizWAdinA raYjayati, anu- (raYj, c. 10.).
To ROUGE , v. a. sOndaryyavarDanArTaM kapolO raYj (c. 10. raYjayati -yituM) or raktavarRIkf or raNgeRa lip.

Rough, a. natonnata, vizama, asama, aSlakzRa. 2 ru(rU)kza, paruza, karkaSa, kaWina, amasfRa, asOmya, amfdu, duHsparSa; (in disposition) nizWura, ugra, kawu, kaWora; (in manners) asaBya, aSizwa, asaMskfta, sTUla, Gana; ‘r(ough) measurement’ sTUlamAnaM. 3 apawu, adakza, anipuRa, akuSala, sTUla. 4 (Sea) kzubDa, taraMgAkula, uttaraMga, vAyukzubDa, pavanAhata. 5 lomaSa, lomAvfta, sTUlaloman; ‘r(ough)-cast’ sTUlaM kxp c. or vi-DA 3 U; ‘r(ough)-draw’ sTUlaM liK 6 P; ‘r(ough)-hew’ sTUlaM takz 1, 5 P or Cid 7 P; ‘r(ough)-rider’ aSvaSikzakaH. [Rough]en, v. t. rUkzI-sTUlI-kf 8 U. [Rough]ly, adv. rukzaM, paruzaM, karkaSaM, sTUlaM, nizWuraM, &c. [Rough]ness, s. vEzamyaM, rukzatA, pAruzyaM, karkaSatvaM, ugratA, kaWoratA, sTUlatA, adakzatA; saMkzoBaH, Urmi-praloWanaM, &c.

ROUGH: I To the touch:(1) banDu(nDu)ra (f. rA);(2) vizama (f. mA), you will have r. steps: padAni Kalu te vizamIBavanti, Sa. iv. 14.;(3) natonnata (f. tA = up and down).II Harsh, severe: q. v.:(1) ru(rU)kza (f. kzA), r. mind: rUkzacetas (mfn.), K.(2) karkaSa (f. SA).III Coarse, clumsy: q. v.: sTUla (f. lA), r. measurement: sTUlamAnam, Li.IV Tempestuous, boisterous: q. v.: kzubDa (f. bDA), saM-, pra-, vi-, r. sea: kzubDArRavaH, V.p.

ROUGH , a. (Not smooth or even) vizamaH -mA -maM, asamaH -mA -maM, asamAnaH -nA -naM, aSlakzRaH -kzRA -kzRaM, rukzaH -kzA -kzaM, rUkzaH -kzA -kzaM. — (Rugged) rukzaH -kzA -kzaM, rUkzaH &c., paruzaH -zA -zaM. — (To the touch) duHsparSaH -rSA -rSaM, duHKasparSaH -rSA -rSaM. — (Harsh, not soft) paruzaH -zA -zaM, rukzaH -kzA -kzaM, rUkzaH &c., paruzavfttiH -ttiH -tti, karkaSaH -SA -SaM, kaWinaH -nA -naM, amfduH -duH -du, amasfRaH -RA -RaM, asOmyaH -myA -myaM, asnigDaH -gDA -gDaM, akomalaH -lA -laM. — (Severe) nizWuraH -rA -raM, karkaSaH -SA -SaM, ugraH -grA -graM, kawuH -wuH -wu, kaWoraH -rA -raM. (Coarse, not finished, not polished) asaMskftaH -tA -taM, apari- zkftaH &c., asaMskAritaH &c., aSizwaH -zwA -zwaM, asaByaH -ByA -ByaM, GanaH -nA -naM, sTUlaH -lA -laM; ‘rough measurement,’ sTUlamAnaM; ‘to measure in a rough way,’ sTUlAntareRa mA. — (Clumsy) sTUlaH -lA -laM, anipuRaH -RA -RaM, adakzaH -kzA -kzaM, akuSalaH -lA -laM, apawuH -wuH -wu. — (With waves or tempest, as the sea) kzubDaH -bDA -bDaM, vyAkzubDaH &c., vikzubDaH &c., saMkzubDaH &c., anilakzubDaH &c., pavanakzubDaH &c., vAyukzubDaH &c., pavanAhataH -tA -taM, taraNgAkulaH -lA -laM, mahAtaraNgaH -NgA -NgaM, vfhattaraNgaH &c., taraNgitaH -tA -taM, velAkulaH -lA -laM; ‘a rough sea,’ kzubDArRavaH, vAyukzubDasamudraH, vAnaM. — (Having a rough or hairy skin) dfQalomA -mA -ma (n), sTUlalomA &c., lomAvftaH -tA -taM, lomaSaH -SA -SaM.
ROUGH-CAST: I Subs.: sTulalepaH (?).II Verb: sTUlalepena limpati, vi-, (lip, c. 6.): v. Also to whitewash.
To ROUGH-CAST , v. a. sTUlAkAreRa kxp (c. 10. kalpayati -yituM), sTUla- rUpeRa kf or nirmA or viDA, sTUlAkAraM dA, sTUlarUpaM kf or dA, sTUla- saMskAraM kf or dA.
ROUGH-DRAUGHT , s. pARquleKyaM, sTUlAleKyaM, pARquleKyamAtraM, vastumAtraM.
ROUGH-DRAW: perh. sTUlam or mandaM liKati, A- (liK, c. 6.).
To ROUGH-DRAW , v. a. sTUlarUpeRa liK (c. 6. liKati -leKituM) or AliK, sTUlAleKyaM kf, pARquleKyaM kf, AleKyAramBaM kf, citrAramBaM kf.
ROUGH-HEW: perh. sTUlaM takzati (takz, c. 1.) or vidaDAti (DA, c. 3.).
To ROUGH-HEW , v. a. sTUlarUpeRa takz (c. 1. takzati -kzituM) or Cid, sTUlAkAraM dA.
ROUGH-HEWN , p. p. sTUlarUpeRa kalpitaH -tA -taM, sTUlAkAreRa tazwaH -zwA -zwaM, asaMskftAkAraH -rA -raM, asaMskftarUpaH -pA -paM, aparizkftAkAraH -rA -raM.
ROUGH-RIDER , s. aSvadamakaH, aSvadamI m. (n). See HORSE-BREAKER.

RUB (v.): I In gen.: Garzati, ut-, ni-, vini-, saM-, (Gfz, c. 1.), r. bed diadems: cUqAmaRiBiru- dGfzwa (f. zwA), R. xvii. 28.; r. bing his ring against a bed of red arsenic: niGfzyANguliM manaHSilA- girO, Ram. ii. 105. 17.II To besmear: q. v.: aByanakti (aYj, c. 7.).III To sham- -poo: q. v.: saMvAhayati (c. of vah).IV To r. down, out, off, away, i. e. to cleanse, erase: q. v.: pra-mArzwi or mArjayati (mfj, c. 2. and c. 10). V To r. off, i. e. wear away: q. v.: kzIyate (pass. of kzI).
RUB (subs.): I The act;(1) GarzaH, -Ram, ni-, vini-, ut-, saM-;(2) saMvAhanam;(3) aByaYjanam; (4) saMmArjanam: for dif.: v. To rub.II Obs- -truction, difficulty: q. v.: antarAyaH.

To RUB , v. a. Gfz (c. 1. Garzati -rzituM), AGfz, nirGfz, mfd (c. 9. mfdnAti mardituM), parimfd, piz (c. 7. pinazwi, pezwuM), pratipiz, nizpiz, GarzaRaM kf, mardanaM kf. — (The body) saMvAh (c. 1. -vAhati, c. 10. -vAhayati -yituM); ‘they both rubbed his feet with their hands,’ karAByAM tasya pAdO saMvavAhatuH; ‘I will rub your feet,’ tava caraRO saMvAhayAmi. — (Rub, so as to clean) mfj (c. 2. mArzwi -rzwuM), pramfj, parimfj, sammfj, avamfj, Amfj, parizkf, prakzal (c. 10. -kzAlayati -yituM), SlakzRIkf. — (Grind in a mortar, &c.) cUrR, cUrRIkf, piz, mfd, kzud, kzodIkf. — (Polish by friction) GarzaRena tij (c. 10. tejayati -yituM) or nizwap or mfj or parizkf. — (Rub one against the other) parasparaM Gfz, parasparaGarzaRaM kf; ‘to rub the hands together,’ karaM kareRa Gfz or nizpiz or pratipiz, pARiM pARO vinizpiz; ‘the teeth to- gether,’ dantAn dantEr Gfz or nizpiz, dantaGarzaRaM kf. — (Rub in, spread over, smear with, as unguents, &c.) lip (c. 6. li- mpati, leptuM), anulip, Alip, aYj, aByaYj, mfd. — (Rub down, as a horse) aSvaloma mfj. — (Rub off) apamfj, avamfj. — (Rub out) apamfj, vyAmfj, pramfj, avamfj, vyAmfS (c. 6. -mfSati -mrazwuM), avamfS, vyAmarzaM kf, avamarzaRaM kf, lopaM kf. — (Rub up) mfj, parizkf.

(Absence of civilization) aSizwatA -tvaM, asaByatA, vidyAhInatA, anakzaratA -tvaM, nirakzaratA -tvaM, vidyASUnyatA, vidyAcA- rahInatA, aparizkAraH. — (Incivility, impoliteness) avinItatA -tvaM, avinayaH, kuSIlatA, duHSIlatA, vAmaSIlatA, aSIlatA, amaryyAdA, durmaryyAdatA, DfzwatA, DArzwyaM, asaByatA, dOrjanyaM, OdDatyaM, ananunayaH, vina- yABAvaH, anAryyatA, adAkziRyaM. — (Roughness, clumsiness) rukzatA, rUkzatA, sTUlatA, adakzatA.

(Destruction) nASaH, vinASaH, praRASaH, kzayaH, DvaMsaH, praDvaMsaH, pariDvaMsaH, parikzayaH, atyayaH, vyasanaM, GAtaH, viGAtaH, lopaH, ucCedaH. — (Defeat, overthrow) parAjayaH, parABavaH, aBiBavaH, sAdaH -danaM, vyasanaM, BaNgaH; ‘of an army,’ balavyasanaM. — (Mischief, bane) kzatiH f., parikzatiH f., dUzaRaM, anizwaM, apAyaH, anarTaH, vizaM. — (Of fortune, estate, &c.) sampattinASaH, sampattiBaNgaH, lakzmIBaNgaH, ESvaryyaBaNgaH, ESvaryyanASaH, parikzIRatA, parikzayaH, astaH -staM; ‘to go to ruin,’ kzi in pass.
